### Meaningful failures and their resolutions

**The invitation integration suite failed once, 22 of 23, and it is not this chunk.** Diagnosed
before retrying, per the working discipline, and the diagnosis is worth keeping because the failure
mode is invisible from the assertion:

```text
✖ grant-platform-admin CLI completes, rejects, and resumes real grants
  SyntaxError: Unexpected token '(', "(node:2309"... is not valid JSON
      at JSON.parse (<anonymous>)
      at runPlatformGrantCli (invitation-acceptance.integration.test.js:1234:15)
      at TestContext.<anonymous> (invitation-acceptance.integration.test.js:534:20)
```

`runPlatformGrantCli` spawns the real `grantPlatformAdmin.js` CLI and **parses its output as
JSON** - `stdout` when it expects exit 0, **`stderr`** when it expects a rejection. The call at
:534 is the rejection case, expecting exit 4. `(node:2309` is Node's own warning prefix,
`(node:<pid>)`, so a Node process warning printed to stderr ahead of the CLI's rejection JSON, and
the parse ate it. **The test is fragile to any warning Node decides to emit**, and only on the
stderr-parsing path - a warning during the exit-0 call goes to stderr where nothing reads it,
which is why one of the two invocations in the same test can break while the other cannot.

**Attribution, and it is not a judgement call.** This chunk changes five files, all Dart or
Markdown; `git diff` over `firestore.rules`, `functions/` and `rules-tests/` prints zero lines,
and the suite compiles `functions/` from unchanged TypeScript through its own `npm run build`.
Nothing in the path this test exercises differs from `1b2b13b`.

**Re-ran the suite plain, as `PLAN.md` documents the command, and the same test passed in
34.6s.** So it is intermittent, not a regression. Two things were checked before concluding
"flake" - running the CLI directly under the same Node printed clean JSON with no warning, and
loading `firebase-admin` under it emitted none either, so the warning belongs to a code path only
the real ineligibility scan reaches, and it is load- or timing-dependent rather than
deterministic. The exact warning was not captured, because the test swallows stderr into the
parse; capturing it means changing `rules-tests`, which is outside this chunk.

**Queued as its own small chunk in `PLAN.md`**, because a suite that fails one run in two on an
unrelated Node warning will eventually be read as a real defect: `runPlatformGrantCli` should
strip warning lines before parsing, or spawn with `NODE_NO_WARNINGS=1`, and the same holds for
the revoke helper beside it.

**One test failure of this chunk's own, and it was the useful kind.** `text.primary` measured 17.147 against
`surface.base` where §2.1 published 17.2, failing the 0.05 tolerance by 0.0028. Resolved by
correcting the document, not by widening the tolerance - see the corrections section. Had the
test merely asserted "clears 4.5:1" the slip would have survived, which is the argument for
asserting published figures.

**Five analyzer diagnostics on the first draft of the token file**, four of them mechanical - a
`library;` directive after its imports, `lerpDuration` not being in `dart:ui` (replaced with
`lerpDouble` over microseconds), an unnecessary `physics.dart` import, and the unused
`sage.100`. The fifth was the `type` override described above, and it arrived as an
`Information`-level "overrides an inherited member" hint rather than as an error, which is
exactly how it would have shipped.

**The first screenshot comparison was wrong and said everything had changed.** It keyed each
image on `FullName.Substring($root.Length + 1)`, and the scratchpad root is an 8.3 short path
whose `FullName` expands differently - so every relative key in the baseline set was cut at the
wrong offset and no two paths matched. Re-keyed on the parent directory name plus the file name.
A comparison that reports "all 101 changed" should be suspected before the change is.

**The NUL-escape check ran over all six touched files and every count was zero.** No digest

## A category is named, and never shown as a document ID - 2026-08-11

### Completed in this session

**Finding 5 from the 2026-08-08 Android run, closed.** No catalog surface states a category
document ID to a person any more. The two the device run named were the import preview, which
told somebody who had typed `Bakery` that their product was "filed under `cat-bakery`", and
"Manage catalog", which listed Charcoal 2kg under `cat-not-cached` because the seed files it
under a category document that does not exist.

It changed `firestore.rules` not at all and nothing in `functions/` either - `git diff` over
both, and over `rules-tests/`, prints **zero lines**. It moved no board row: a defect repair
inside rows that were already green has no colour to move.

### The queued chunk's premise was wrong twice, and checking it was the finding

`PLAN.md` queued this as two surfaces and attached a shape: "Find the existing resolution first
and reuse it. Three copies of 'look up a category name' is how the third one drifts." Both
halves of the premise are false against source, and the second one changed the work.

1. **The read-only catalog had the identical fallback.** `tenant_catalog.dart:346` read
   `categoryNames[product.categoryId] ?? product.categoryId`, which is character for character
   what the two named surfaces read. It looked correct on the device because every product seen
   through it was filed under a category that page had read. So it was not a surface that got it
   right; it was a surface the defect had not been triggered on.
2. **The resolution that does exist is in reporting, and it is not this one.**
   `SalesTotalsCategoryOptions.nameOf` answers `String?`, and `sales_totals_panel.dart:437`
   words the null case as `'one category'` under a comment reading "an ID with no name is not
   shown as a label of its own". That is the precedent and the right instinct, in a different
   area, with a different and also-correct degrade policy: it drops the label rather than naming
   an unnameable category.
3. **Eight places name a category, seven of them reachable, and every one of them could state an
   ID** - six through a `?? id` fallback and two by printing it outright - through **five**
   copies of the same lookup. Counted before anything was written:

| Where | What it did | Reached by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Read-only catalog list | `?? id` | a product filed off the categories page |
| "Manage catalog" list | `?? id` | **finding 5's second half** - `cat-not-cached` |
| "Manage catalog" → "Filed under X." | `?? id` | unreachable: the ID comes from the chip row |
| "Correct" dialog, category-off sentence | the ID, always | any product filed off the page |
| The correction confirmation, "Category: was ..." | its own inline loop, `?? id` | moving a product out of a category filed off the page |
| Bulk selection list | `?? id` | a product filed off the categories page |
| Bulk correction report, "was → now" | `?? id` | the same |
| Import preview, "filed under ..." | the ID, always | **finding 5's first half** |

### One answer, and two wordings of it

`tenantCategoryNames`, `tenantCategoryLabel` and `tenantCategoryPhrase` sit in
`lib/tenancy/tenant_catalog.dart` beside `TenantCategory`, which is the file that defines what a
category is and the file every one of those surfaces already imports. Modelled on
`tenantStaffLabel` in `tenant_staff_names.dart`, which is the same problem for a different
identity - and the doc comment records where the two deliberately disagree: **a staff label keeps
the UID visible even beside a resolved name**, because a UID is what every sale, shift and audit
record is attributed by and a person reading a history needs it. Nothing a person ever sees
refers to a category by its ID.

The guarantees are settled, not open:

1. **A document ID is not a name and is never shown as one.** Five copies of the lookup answered
   eight places and every one of them could print the ID; there is now one resolution, and the ID
   has no path to a screen from any catalog surface. Two widget tests assert it over **every `Text` in the tree** rather than over
   the slot that was wrong, matching `cat-` and `ct_` - the seeded shape and the shape
   `buildCategoryIntent` derives - because the two defective surfaces were precisely the two
   nobody was looking at.
2. **The unlisted state stays legible rather than being hidden.** `cat-not-cached` was not bad
   data: it is a product filed under a category this surface cannot read, and a blank would have
   deleted the fact. It reads **"Category not listed here"**, which is true of both causes and
   claims neither. The two causes are indistinguishable from the client - a business holding more
   categories than one bounded page, and a category document that cannot be read at all - so the
   wording says only what is known.
3. **The import preview names what the sheet said, in three descending degrees of certainty.**
   The categories this surface read first, because they are the list every other catalog surface
   names a category from; then the row's own `categoryName`, which is a true name because the
   server matched it against a real category in order to accept the row at all; then the unlisted
   phrase. **The document ID is not a third degree - it is not shown at all.** The row's own name
   is second rather than first because the fold is case-insensitive, so what somebody typed can
   differ in case from what is stored.
4. **The import's wording is held with its plan.** `_importCategoryNames` is captured when the
   preview is built and cleared by `_discardPlan` with everything else, because a commit re-sends
   the pages the preview sent and must word their rows identically, while the route re-reads its
   categories between the two. A bulk correction needs no equivalent: its rows carry the wording
   they were planned with, inside the immutable page.
5. **Two wordings for one answer, and the split is grammar rather than taste.**
   `tenantCategoryLabel` opens a line - a list row does not begin in lower case - and
   `tenantCategoryPhrase` sits inside a sentence, because "filed under Category not listed here"
   is not a sentence anybody wrote. Both are asserted, so a later edit cannot quietly make them
   one.
6. **A recorded decision was reversed on purpose.** "Stating the ID beats stating nothing"
   appeared as a comment in `bulk_catalog.dart` and in `catalog_management.dart`, and as the
   reason on a test in `bulk_catalog_test.dart`. All three now say the opposite, in the words
   `design.md` §8 rule 1 asks for: name things the way the shopkeeper does, never the way the
   system does. The old reading was defensible when a surface had nothing better; what it missed
   is that the ID is not a worse name, it is not a name.
7. **Reporting was left alone, deliberately.** `SalesTotalsCategoryOptions.nameOf` is correct and
   its `'one category'` is right for a filter label, where naming an unlisted category would be
   noise about something the reader did not ask about. Converting it would have changed a working
   surface in another area to make one count smaller. Six resolution paths became two, and the
   second is that one.
8. **No behaviour changed anywhere.** No repository call, no state logic, no routing condition,
   no payload. `describeImportOutcomes` gained a named parameter and `_runImport` gained one;
   every wire payload in the diff is byte-identical, and the panel tests that assert
   `payloads.last['rows'] == payloads.first['rows']` still pass unchanged.

### Deliberately not done

- **`lib/checkout/checkout_cart_panel.dart` was not touched.** The till resolves categories
  through the Hive snapshot's `categoryById` and words the unresolved case as an "Other" chip, so
  it renders no ID and has no defect. It is also another session's unstaged file.
- **No token from `lib/ui/tokens.dart` was read**, per the chunk's own exclusion: a wording
  repair is not the step that starts reading them, and a half-migrated surface is worse than an
  unmigrated one.
- **Finding 4 was not touched.** The add-product form's missing picker is recorded against the
  redesign's step 3, which rewrites that form.
- **No server file, no rule, no `rules-tests` file, no deployment.** `importProducts` echoing the
  `categoryId` it wrote is correct of the server - the ID is what it wrote - and every repair
  here is on the reading side.
- **Category rename and delete stay unoffered**, for the orphaning reason, and the import still

## The ripple dies at the theme - 2026-08-11

### Completed in this session

**`design.md` §11 step 2**, and the first redesign step that changes anything a person can see.
`splashFactory: NoSplash.splashFactory` on `ThemeData`, `overlayColor` on the four button themes
reading §2.1's action tiers out of the token layer, `useMaterial3: true` stated rather than
inherited, and `SpiritScrollBehavior` carrying §2.4's bouncing physics with no overscroll glow.
One theme file, one line in `lib/main.dart`, **zero call sites**.

It changed `firestore.rules` not at all and nothing in `functions/` either - `git diff` over both
prints **zero lines**. It moved no board row and no rollout step; what it moved is the **Design
system** track, 8% to 15%.

### Why this was the chunk, and why App Check was passed over a fourth time

The previous session queued the App Check research here on this file's own instruction: the
device findings had run out, it is the only queued item that would move a red row, and `PLAN.md`
said it "should not be passed over a fourth time without a reason better than ordering". **The
product owner asked why the reskin chunks were not being taken and redirected to them.** That is
a decision rather than drift and it is recorded in `PLAN.md` beside the chunk, so the next session
reads a call and not an oversight. Three frictions were put to them before the redirect and none
was contradicted: step 2 cannot be verified without a device run, the whole design system lives in
untracked files, and step 4 needs a border-contrast answer that does not exist yet.

### §2.4's instruction is wrong about this codebase, and the audit already knew

§2.4 says to replace `InkWell` with an opacity-and-scale overlay. There is exactly **one**
`InkWell` in the migrated tree (`checkout_cart_panel.dart:1029`); every other ripple in the app
comes from Material's own `FilledButton`, `OutlinedButton`, `TextButton`, `IconButton`,
`ChoiceChip`, `ListTile` and `SegmentedButton`. `DESIGN-AUDIT.md` §4.5 found that and §6 decision
4 split the work rather than choosing between the two options it posed:

- **Step 2** kills the ripple at the theme. One file, zero call sites.
- **Step 3** builds `PressSurface` inside `AppButton`, so the scale-0.97 `spring.snappy` press
  arrives at the moment every call site is already being rewritten.

The arithmetic is the argument: there are **zero `AnimationController`s in the migrated tree**, so
a step-2 call-site sweep would build the spring substrate, touch ~40 sites, and touch all of them
again in step 3.

### The guarantees

1. **One line reaches every ripple**, because `InkResponse` falls back to
   `ThemeData.splashFactory` and the M3 button defaults delegate to it explicitly.
2. **`useMaterial3: true` is load-bearing, not decoration.** The Material 2 paths in
   `outlined_button.dart` and `text_button.dart` **hardcode** `InkRipple.splashFactory`, so
   flipping that flag would silently restore ripples on two of the four tiers. It was previously
   unset, which means true by default; a test now asserts it beside the splash factory.
3. **The four button themes are the first thing in the app to read the token layer.** Filled and
   elevated are `action.primary`, outlined is `action.secondary`, text is `action.tertiary`.
   `AppActionRole.hoverFill()` and `pressedFill()` answer §2.1's **two** different rules - the
   primary tier moves its container to named colours, the other three wash their own label at 8%
   and 12% - so `_pressOverlay` does not have to know which kind of tier it holds. That method
   pair was built by step 1 for exactly this and had no caller until now.
4. **The label repoint did not come with the overlay.** The outlined button is still mint where
   §2.1 wants sage, and `test/ui/tokens_test.dart` still asserts that divergence. It closes in
   step 3, when `AppButton` rewrites the call sites, so its image diff has one cause.
5. **Focus resolves to the hover wash, and that is deliberately not §2.1's focus row.** §2.1 gives
   focus-visible a 2px ring at 2px offset - a border, not an overlay - which belongs to `AppButton`
   and to §9's audit in step 12. The thing a `WidgetStateProperty` must not do meanwhile is answer
   `null` for a focused button: that paints no overlay at all and would leave a keyboard user with
   *less* feedback than before this step.
6. **`action.destructive` has no Material theme to attach to** and arrives with `AppButton`.
7. **Scroll physics live on the app, not on each scrollable**, because §2.4 says *everywhere* and
   that is not a rule three hundred list views can be trusted to remember. `MaterialScrollBehavior`
   is extended rather than replaced, so desktop scrollbars and the drag-device set are untouched.

### Two screenshots moved, and neither of them shows a ripple

Both are `31b-a-receipt-found`, mobile and web. **The visible difference is the receipt field's
text caret**, present in the baseline and absent now.

The mechanism is the harness rather than the app. That capture case ends its `afterPump` with
`await tester.tap(find.text('Find receipt'))` and **no `pumpAndSettle`**, so the shot lands
wherever the frame timeline happens to be. With a ripple in flight the binding kept pumping frames
and the caret was captured in its "on" blink phase; with no ripple the tree settles immediately
and the caret is captured "off".

**It is attributable and it is not evidence.** Two consecutive runs of identical code hash
identically, so the pair really did move because of this change - but a ripple exists only
mid-press and a glow only mid-drag, so what this step did cannot appear in a still image at all.
Recorded in `PLAN.md` as a standing trap, because **step 3's springs will move that pair again**
and the next session should read what differs before attributing it.

### Deliberately not done

- **No call site was touched**, and no `PressSurface` was built. Both belong to step 3.
- **No label, radius, or fill was repointed.** The four divergences step 1 asserted are still
  asserted; only the overlay and the splash factory moved.
- **Two rows of §2.1's own state table are not implemented here**, and saying "the state table"
  without naming them would overstate the chunk. **Disabled** - container `#1E3A2B`, label
  `#5D7468` - still resolves through `styleFrom`'s Material defaults, and **loading** - the
  container held, the label replaced by a 16px spinner, the width frozen - has no expression in a
  `ButtonStyle` at all. Both are `AppButton`'s, which is why `AppActionRoles` already carries
  `disabledContainer`, `disabledLabel`, `disabledBorder` and `loadingIndicatorSize` with no reader.
  What step 2 implements is the **hover and pressed rows**, plus a focus fallback that is not the
  focus row.
- **No route transition.** §11 step 2 names them, and §2.4 requires anything spatial to be a
  **spring** that retargets from its current position and velocity. A `PageTransitionsBuilder`
  written on a duration would satisfy the step number while contradicting the section it comes
  from, so it waits for the substrate `AppButton` builds. **This is the one part of step 2 that is
  not finished**, and it is named here rather than left as an implied completion.
- **The single `InkWell`**, the chips, and the `ListTile`s keep their own press treatment until
  their steps arrive (7, 3-4, and 6 respectively), per decision 4's straggler list.
- **No server file, no rule, no deployment.**

                         explaining why step 2 is theme-level)
lib/main.dart           (one line: scrollBehavior)
test/theme_test.dart    (+5)

### Test commands and results

| Suite | Command | Result |

| Functions / Rules / Reconciliation / Invitations | carried | **409 / 161 / 10 / 23** |

`flutter analyze --no-pub test/theme_test.dart lib/theme.dart lib/main.dart`: **one issue, and it
is the pre-existing Sentry `profilesSampleRate` warning** this file has carried since before the
migration. Nothing new.

**The four non-Flutter suites were carried for the second consecutive chunk**, on the same
reasoning as the first: two Dart files and one test file changed, `git diff` over
`firestore.rules`, `functions/` and `rules-tests/` prints zero lines, and no suite among the four
can observe a Dart file. **`PLAN.md` now names two consecutive carries as the limit** - a third
should measure them, on the same reasoning that made the third consecutive unreachable callable a
surface instead. This is the **twelfth** consecutive chunk to leave `firestore.rules`
byte-identical.

**What the five new tests do and do not prove.** They assert at the `InkWell` the button actually
builds rather than at the `ButtonStyle`, because what could go wrong here is the merge: a button
resolves its widget style over the theme's over the M3 defaults, and a theme-level property that
loses that race is invisible from the theme object alone. They also carry a **control** - the same
list tree without `SpiritScrollBehavior`, asserting that it does *not* bounce and *does* build an
overscroll indicator - so the two positive assertions cannot pass against a change that did
nothing. What none of them prove is how any of it feels. Per `design.md` §10 that is a device
check with the performance overlay on, and the session instruction skipped the Android build, so
**nobody has looked at this**. The debt is now five chunks deep and step 2 is the one entry in it
that has no other way to be verified.

### Meaningful failures and their resolutions

**One test failed on the first run, and the assertion was wrong rather than the code.**

```text
Expected: <Instance of 'BouncingScrollPhysics'>
  Actual: AlwaysScrollableScrollPhysics:<AlwaysScrollableScrollPhysics -> BouncingScrollPhysics
          -> RangeMaintainingScrollPhysics>
```

`ScrollView` **prepends** `AlwaysScrollableScrollPhysics` to whatever the behaviour supplied, so a
position holds a chain rather than the type the behaviour named, and `isA<BouncingScrollPhysics>()`
over the outermost link is an assertion that can only ever fail. The test now walks
`ScrollPhysics.parent` and says why at the helper.

**Two `const` expressions that are not.** `AppTokens.dark.colors.action` cannot be `const` - a
property access is not a constant expression, which is a rule about the expression rather than
about the value, since `AppTokens.dark` is canonicalized. Both the theme and the test hold it as
`final`, and the theme says so at the declaration.

**Four Dart string literals were terminated early by an apostrophe.** `'... the tier's overlay'`
ends the string at `tier`, and the analyzer's cascade of "Expected to find ','" points at the
consequences rather than the cause. Reworded rather than escaped, because a test name reading
"the fills of its own tier" is no worse than one with a backslash in it.

**The NUL-escape check ran over all five touched files and every count was zero.**

## The working tree is emptied into the repository - 2026-08-11

### Completed in this session

**Not a chunk.** The product owner asked why so much was uncommitted, and then had it committed.
Four commits, no new code, and the last of them makes the Flutter baseline honest for the first
time since 2026-08-10.

```text
1262476  design.md, DESIGN-AUDIT.md, claude.md, docs/printer_transport.md   (2,001 lines)
64d27b1  tool/screenshots/, six files - the harness, without its output     (2,899 lines)
2942214  lib/ui/records.dart, three panels, ten test files                  (1,600 / -298)
   +one  .gitignore for the generated output, plus PLAN.md and this entry
```

### What was actually there, established rather than assumed

The question was asked about "tenancy files", and the first useful answer was that they were
**modified, not untracked**, and were not seven separate edits. `tenant_staff_directory.dart` had
been rewritten to render a `TenantStatStrip` above a `LayoutBuilder` choosing a table or cards by
width; that pushed tap targets below the fold in the test viewport, so seven invitation suites
were mechanically refactored onto `ensureVisible` helpers. One widget change, ten files.

The provenance, from dates rather than from the log:

- **`1b2b13b` (2026-08-10 17:22) committed `lib/theme.dart` and nothing else**, and its message
  states "Flutter holds at 1524".
- **`lib/ui/records.dart` was written at 18:26 the same evening** - an hour after that commit -
  and never produced one of its own. `screenshots.zip` followed at 22:04, then `claude.md`
  (09:20), `DESIGN-AUDIT.md` (10:01) and `design.md` (10:29) the next morning, and the first
  commit after all of it was the token layer at 11:16, which staged only its own file.
- **`HISTORY.md` has no entry for that session.** Every mention of `records.dart` in this log is
  retrospective, written by a later session noting that it was untracked.

**Why it was left is not recorded and is not reconstructed here.** What can be said is what made
it *stick*: the working discipline says to stage only the scoped files, which is what keeps a
chunk reviewable and is also why **work arriving outside a chunk has no path to a commit at
all**. Four consecutive chunks read it as another session's, wrote a line saying so, and stepped
around it. The one inference worth recording is that the governing documents were uncommitted
too - a session following that workflow commits its own documents - which suggests the design
system was not built as a numbered chunk under it.

### Why it stopped being tolerable

`DESIGN-AUDIT.md` §4.7 records a conflict between `records.dart`'s stated design and `design.md`
§4.3 - whether a component or its caller decides what a compact rendering loses - and §6 decision
2 **resolved it in `records.dart`'s favour**, quoting `records.dart:375-380`. So a design decision
had been taken in favour of a file that was not in the repository, citing line numbers no
checkout carried. Redesign steps 3 and 6 rewrite that same territory, and step 3 is the queued
chunk, so the collision was one session away.

### Reviewed rather than adopted on trust

It is not this session's code, and 1,143 lines of somebody else's went in under this session's
name, so it was checked rather than accepted because the suite was green:

- **No repository call, gateway, callable or submission path is touched in any of the three
  panels.** The sale panel's hunks all sit inside `_CartEditorState`'s build region and **move**
  `_saleSection`, `_tenderSection` and `_saveSection` into a layout wrapper without changing what
  they call. Its one new computation sums the cart's quantities for a badge.
- **The overridden `setState`** bumps a `ValueNotifier` because the compact layout puts the cart
  in a modal sheet, which is its own route and does not rebuild with the parent element. That is
  presentation plumbing, and it is the one thing in the diff that looks like state logic and is
  not.
- **No permission guard was dropped while a list became a table.** Four `allowedRoles` and two
  `canAccess` in `tenant_staff_directory.dart`, counted against `HEAD` and against the working
  tree: identical.
- `flutter analyze` over `records.dart`, the three panels, every test beside them and the
  harness: **no issues**.

It is a **partial** migration - three of the twenty `*_panel.dart` files in the tree - and is
committed as one rather than dressed up as a finished sweep.

### The generated screenshots are ignored, and the reason is in `.gitignore`

The harness is source and is tracked; its 101 images are not. `fakes.dart` derives its business
dates from `DateTime.now()` deliberately, because the daily summary and reconciliation compute a
business date the same way and read by exact path, so a hardcoded date would render those screens
permanently empty. Re-running on another day therefore moves about **39 of the 101 images** with
no code change behind any of them, measured earlier the same day. Tracking the output would put
those 39 into every future diff. `screenshots.zip` (9.5 MB of the same output) and the
`.codex-*.png` scratch captures from 2026-08-03 are ignored with it.

## `AppButton`, and the spring substrate under it - 2026-08-11

`design.md` §11 step 3, first half. The first component in this app's history that a call
site can reach, and the first spring anywhere in the migrated tree.

### The chunk was re-scoped before it started, because its own description was wrong

`PLAN.md` queued this as "the call-site migration is mechanical - roughly forty buttons".
Counted against source, the migrated tree (everything outside `lib/pos/**`, `lib/screens/**`,
`lib/services/**`, `lib/api/**` and `lib/widgets/**`) holds **168** `FilledButton` /
`OutlinedButton` / `TextButton` / `ElevatedButton` constructor calls across **38 files**, plus
13 `IconButton`s. That is four times the queued figure and it decides what fits in a session.

The product owner was asked and chose: **build the component and migrate one complete area**,
`tenant_routing_shell.dart`'s 22 sites, leaving 146 across 37 files as the next chunk. They
also moved **route transitions out of this chunk**.

### Route transitions are their own chunk now, and the reason is a framework fact

`PLAN.md` carried step 2's unfinished fourth part into this chunk on the reasoning that a
spring transition needs the substrate `AppButton` builds. The substrate is now built and the
transition still does not fit, for a reason worth recording:

**A `PageTransitionsBuilder` cannot produce a spring.** It only reshapes an animation the
route already drives on a duration, so anything written through `pageTransitionsTheme` -
which is the one mechanism reaching every `MaterialPageRoute` without touching a call site -
is a curve wearing a spring's name. A real one needs a `PageRoute` subclass driving its own
controller with a `SpringSimulation`, plus swapping the **22** `MaterialPageRoute` call sites
in the migrated tree, plus care on the pop path so the route still finalizes. That is a chunk,
not a rider.

### What was built

**`lib/ui/spring.dart` - `SpringDrive`.** An unbounded `AnimationController` plus one method,
`animateTo`, which always reads the live value and the live velocity out of the controller it
is retargeting. `forward()` is deliberately neither wrapped nor exposed: it is the API that
would satisfy a spring-shaped call site while doing the one thing §2.4 forbids. Unbounded
because a spring overshoots, and a bounded controller would let the clamp rather than the
physics decide what `spring.bouncy` looks like.

The drive runs a **normalized 0-to-1 progress** and the widget lerps the quantity off it. That
is not tidiness: `SpringSimulation` decides it is done against `Tolerance`, whose defaults are
absolute, and a press travelling from scale 1.0 to 0.97 is a 0.03-wide journey that finishes
inside the tolerance it is measured with.

**`lib/ui/press.dart` - `PressSurface`.** §2.4's replacement for the ink ripple: scale 0.97 on
`spring.snappy`, plus §2.1's hover and pressed overlays, plus §9's focus ring. Three things in
it are decisions rather than code:

1. **The ring's 4px gutter is reserved always**, not painted on focus. A ring at a 2px offset
   needs 4px outside the shape; painting it only when focused reflows the row the moment a
   keyboard user tabs into it, which is a worse accessibility failure than the one §9 asks to
   fix.
2. **`focus-visible`, not `focused`.** The ring reads `FocusManager.instance.highlightMode`,
   which is where `InkResponse` reads it, so a migrated control and an unmigrated one beside
   it agree about when a ring appears. A tap that happens to focus a button draws nothing.
3. **The spring is created on first press**, not on first build, so a screen full of buttons
   nobody has touched holds no tickers.

**`lib/ui/buttons.dart` - `AppButton`.** Four tiers by three sizes. `action.destructive` had no
Material button theme to attach to and therefore could not be rendered anywhere in this app
until now. Loading freezes the width by leaving the label laid out and unpainted rather than by
measuring it - a measured width is a second source of truth that goes stale when the text scale
changes.

**The painted height and the tap target are separate things**, which is what lets §5.2's `sm`
(32h) and §9's 48dp coexist. §9 is pass/fail under `claude.md` hard rule 6; §5.2 gives three
sizes; only separating them satisfies both.

### Three defects found by testing, all of them in code written this session

**The 48dp tap target was reserved and dead.** The min-target `ConstrainedBox` sat *outside*
the `GestureDetector`, so the extra area was laid out and answered nothing: a tap two pixels
inside the top edge of a 32-high button hit padding. **A size assertion passed against this** -
`getSize` reported 48 - which is exactly the kind of pass that ships a defect. The box now sits
inside the detector, and the test taps all four edges instead of measuring.

**A press callback read `MediaQuery` off `context`.** A pointer still down when its tree is
torn down - a route popped mid-press, or a test releasing a held gesture in a tear-down -
delivers its `up` to a **deactivated** element, and the lookup throws "Looking up a deactivated
widget's ancestor is unsafe". The tokens and the reduced-motion flag are now read in `build`
and held, which also registers the dependency properly.

**A too-long label overflowed its own button by 39px** on the landing route at phone width.
See the misattribution below.

### One fix was attributed to the wrong change, and the correction matters

The first run of the shell's tests produced `RenderFlex overflowed by 99200 pixels` and
`199200 pixels`. Those were attributed to `Flexible` inside the button's label `Row` under the
unbounded constraints an `AppBar`'s actions hand out, and `Flexible` was made conditional.

**That was wrong.** The real cause was in the same batch of failures: `AppTokens.of` threw for
every one of those buttons, and Flutter substitutes an `ErrorWidget` for a build that throws.
An `ErrorWidget` in a `Row` is what produced the six-figure overflow numbers. Both changes
landed together and the fix was credited to the wrong one.

The cost of that mistake was two further failures. Dropping `Flexible` let a long label
overflow a narrow slot; replacing it with a `LayoutBuilder` fixed that and broke every parent
that measures **intrinsic** width - `AlertDialog` puts its actions in an `OverflowBar`, which
does, and the failure is a bare `hasSize` assertion naming the dialog rather than the button.

**The correct answer is what Material already does**: `Flexible` unconditionally. `RenderFlex`
permits flex under unbounded constraints when `mainAxisSize` is `min` and rejects it only when
`max` - which here is `expand`, where the width is bounded by construction. Both hazards now
have tests: a 120px slot, and a real `AlertDialog`.

### The token layer learned to answer without a theme, and that was a real decision

`AppTokens.of` throws when the extension is absent, decided in step 1 so a nested `Theme` built
from a fresh `ThemeData` could not silently render a compact screen at comfortable spacing.
Correct for a screen; wrong for a component. **46 of the widget-test files build their own bare
`ThemeData`**, and under `of` every one of them is a crash the moment a migrated widget appears
in it - which would make "remember `theme: spiritTheme`" a rule to be remembered at ~50 sites
and at every new one.

`AppTokens.componentOf` falls back to `AppTokens.dark`. **The fallback is safe in the one
direction that matters**: `dark` carries `AppDensity.comfortable`, the *stricter* density on
every dimension §9 measures - 48x48 targets rather than 32x32, larger rows, larger body text.
A component that falls back can render a compact screen at comfortable size, a cosmetic fault,
and can never shrink a tap target below §9's floor. What it cannot catch is stated in the
accessor's own doc: a nested `Theme` built from a fresh `ThemeData` loses its density silently,
which is why `of` still exists and still throws.

### The two divergences closed, and a third was taken deliberately

`test/ui/tokens_test.dart` had asserted two values as divergences *on purpose* since step 1, so
the step closing one would fail a test rather than pass quietly. It worked exactly as designed:
both moved, the test failed, and the rows were rewritten as agreements in the same change.

- The outlined button's label, mint to `action.secondary` sage `#B8D6C5`.
- The primary label, `bgDark` to `#0A0F0C`, through `colorScheme.onPrimary` and `onSecondary`.
- **And a third that was not on the list**: the outlined button's border, `mutedGreen`
  `#1E3A2B` to `action.secondary.border` `#2C5340`. Taken because an unmigrated
  `OutlinedButton` and an `AppButton` in `secondary` sitting on the same screen must not
  disagree about the same tier, and each half would have looked individually defensible in
  review.

### `spring.snappy` overshoots, and the document is generous about it

Measured while writing the tests. Damping ratios: `snappy` **0.821**, `smooth` 1.012, `gentle`
1.014, `bouncy` 0.558. §2.4 says "All are critically or near-critically damped except
`spring.bouncy`", which is true of `smooth` and `gentle` - both a shade *past* critical - and
generous about `snappy`, which is underdamped and overshoots by **1.1%**.

Not a defect and no value was changed: 1.1% of a press journey is 0.0003 of scale, for one
frame, on a 48px button. `bouncy` overshoots by **12%**, an order of magnitude more, which is
the distinction §6.2's reward layer rests on. The ratios are now asserted so "near-critically"
cannot quietly cover a different spring later.

### The state matrix

`claude.md` hard rule 5 and §10 both require it. **Six of §5's nine states, and the other three
are absent on purpose**: `error` belongs to `AppTextField` per §5.2 - a button has no value to
be wrong about - a button that may not be used is `disabled` rather than read-only, and there
is no such thing as an empty button.

How each state is produced matters, because a faked state proves nothing. `enabled`, `disabled`
and `loading` are properties, so each is one capture of the whole 4x3 grid. `pressed` holds
four simultaneous **touch** pointers, one per tier. `hover` is one capture per tier -
`MouseTracker` asserts on a second simultaneous **mouse** pointer, and because the tracker
lives on the binding rather than on the test, that failure poisons the next capture in the same
file. `focus-visible` is one capture per tier because only one node can hold the primary focus,
and it needs `FocusHighlightStrategy.alwaysTraditional` or the ring is correctly suppressed on
a test binding's touch platform and the picture shows its absence.

**The press captures are the only place a spring is visible in this harness, and they are still
not evidence about motion.** They photograph the scale at a settled moment. Whether the spring
is interruptible, and whether it drops a frame, is a device check.

## Every remaining button becomes an `AppButton` - 2026-08-11

`design.md` §11 step 3's first half, finished. The component landed earlier the same day with
22 of its call sites migrated; this chunk took the other **133, across 35 files**, and the
migrated tree now holds **155 `AppButton` call sites and 7 Material buttons**.

### The count was wrong again, in the other direction this time

The previous session corrected "roughly forty buttons" to 168. **168 was also wrong**, by 8:
`lib/config.dart` is a **fully commented-out file** - all 8 of its "call sites" are inside `//`
lines, and its only importer is `lib/screens/main_hub_screen.dart`, which `claude.md` hard rule 3
makes read-only. A count that greps source without excluding comments finds work that does not
exist. The real figure was **162**, and it is now 155 migrated plus 7 deliberately left.

**The 7 left are `checkout_cart_panel.dart`'s**, and they are step 7's rather than skipped: that
is the sale path, where §2.1's rule that *Clear this sale* is destructive and *Save sale* is
primary has to be applied, and applying it here would have put a step-7 decision inside a step-3
diff.

### The sweep was mechanical; the tier decisions were not

A balanced-paren rewriter handled the regular shapes and **refused 17 sites it was not certain
about**, which is the part worth keeping: a regex would have rewritten them wrongly and silently.
Every refusal turned out to be a real decision.

**Fifteen call sites were hand-rolling §2.1's loading row.** The shape was always the same - swap
the icon for a 16px `CircularProgressIndicator`, change the label to a gerund, and null
`onPressed`:

```dart
onPressed: _submitting ? null : _submit,
icon: _submitting ? const SizedBox.square(dimension: 16, child: ...) : const Icon(...),
label: Text(_submitting ? 'Archiving...' : 'Archive business'),
```

They are now `loading: _submitting` with `onPressed: _submit` left intact. **Dropping the
`? null :` is the part that matters and it is not a simplification**: `AppButton` renders a null
callback as §2.1's *disabled* row, so keeping it would have painted "you may not do this" over a
control whose truth is "this is happening". `AppButton` suppresses the press itself while
loading, so the guard survives without the wrong colours - and the width freezes, which the
hand-rolled version never did, so those buttons used to resize under the finger as the label

**`action.destructive` found its call sites, and one of them is why the tier exists.**
`tenant_staff_invitation_cancellation.dart` reached past the theme for

**`Correct` / `Retire` closes both halves of a §9 failure.** §9 lists it twice: "20px targets on

**Pagination stopped being a primary action.** `Next page` was a `FilledButton` on six feeds while

## A route arrives on a spring - 2026-08-12

`design.md` §11 step 2's fourth and last part, and with it **step 2 is finished**. `AppPageRoute`
drives its own controller with a `SpringSimulation` on `spring.smooth`, and all **23**
`MaterialPageRoute` call sites in the migrated tree are now it. §6.2's two route rows are both
implemented: horizontal with a 30% parallax below `tenantTableBreakpoint`, fade-through on
`motion.medium` at or above it.

### `PLAN.md` predicted a leak that this SDK cannot produce, and the correction matters

The chunk was scoped around a framework fact: `AnimationController.animateWith` always reports
direction *forward*, so a simulation driven to 0 finishes `completed` rather than `dismissed`,
`TransitionRoute._handleStatusChanged` never calls `finalizeRoute`, and every popped route leaks.
That was true of the API this file had in mind. **On Flutter 3.44 `TransitionRoute` takes the
simulation itself**: `createSimulation({required bool forward})` is called on every push and pop,
and the pop path hands the result to `AnimationController.animateBackWith`, which sets the reverse
direction. So the hand-rolled `didPush` / `didPop` override the chunk was sized for was not
written at all.

**Two consequences, and the second is the better one.** The route is about 80 lines of code
rather than 250. And **interruptibility comes free and correct**: `createSimulation` is called
*before* the controller is stopped, so `controller.value` and `controller.velocity` inside it are
the live figures of the transition still in flight. A pop arriving mid-push leaves from where the
page actually is, at the speed it is actually going.

The leak was still verified rather than assumed - `routes_test.dart` pushes and pops a hundred
times and waits on `Route.completed` for every one, because that future resolves in
`TransitionRoute.dispose`, which only runs if the navigator finalized the route.

### `SettlingSpringSimulation`, and why the plain one is not enough for a route

`SpringSimulation` decides it is done against `Tolerance`, whose defaults are absolute, and
`AnimationController` keeps whatever the simulation last reported. So a spring driven to 1 stops
at about `0.999`. On a press that is three hundred-thousandths of a scale factor. **On a route it
is a whole page parked a fraction of a pixel off its own edge for as long as it is on screen**,
and a page on a fractional offset renders every glyph on one.

`SettlingSpringSimulation` wraps the spring and reports the exact end once `isDone` is true.
`spring_test.dart` measures both: the plain simulation's last position is `isNot(1.0)` and within
`1e-3` of it, the wrapped one's is `1.0`, and every frame before that is identical between the two
so the wrapper cannot become a second set of physics.

**`SpringDrive` deliberately still uses the plain one.** The 114 screenshots were captured against
it and swapping it under them would move a set of images for a difference nobody can see. Recorded
in the class doc as a safe change for whichever chunk regenerates them anyway.

### The delegated transition was built, measured, and taken out again

**This is the finding of the session.** `MaterialApp.home` builds the landing route as a
`MaterialPageRoute`, and `MaterialRouteTransitionMixin.canTransitionTo` refuses to animate a route
out under one it does not recognise **unless that route offers a `delegatedTransition`**. Eight of
the twenty-three pushes leave the landing route, so without one they slide in over a surface that
does not move.

It was implemented, and it worked, and it cost **an extra Firestore read on every push and every
pop**:

```text
with    delegatedTransition:  sales, returns, sales
without delegatedTransition:  sales, returns
```

The mechanism, because the four failing tests named none of it. `ModalRoute.didChangeNext` sets
`receivedTransition` when the incoming route offers one; `_buildFlexibleTransitions` then wraps
the covered route's own transition in it. That changes the **shape** of the widget tree above the
page, so the page - which hangs off `route._subtreeKey`, a `GlobalKey` - is re-parented rather
than updated. A re-parented subtree rebuilds. `_TenantSaleHistoryPanelState.build` hands
`TenantRouteGuard` a **fresh `load` closure** on every rebuild, and the guard's `didUpdateWidget`
compares `oldWidget.load != widget.load` **by identity**, so it reloads.

`claude.md` hard rule 1 - a UI change never issues a repository call - decides it on its own. The
parallax therefore stops at the boundary between the two route kinds: the 15 pushes that cover
another `AppPageRoute` parallax through `buildTransitions`, and the 8 that cover the landing route
do not. **Both halves are asserted**, so the day the coupling is closed and the delegated
transition goes back in, the test that pins the boundary fails and is rewritten in the same
change.

**The coupling is a latent defect that predates this chunk**, and it is not repaired here because
repairing it is a behaviour change: any rebuild of any of these panels, from any cause, already
re-queries. It is recorded in `PLAN.md` as its own queued item.

### §4.1's third breakpoint is not named by §6.2, and the reading is recorded rather than assumed

§6.2's route rows name `compact` and `expanded`. §4.1 defines three names, and `medium` - 768 to
1023 - appears in neither row. The literal reading is taken: `expanded` is `>= 1024`, so
everything below it gets the compact row, which is also the grouping §4.3 uses when it leaves the
sale on one pane at medium. Asserted at 400, 900, 1024 and 1200 rather than left to inference.

**No fourth breakpoint constant was declared.** `tenantTableBreakpoint` in `lib/ui/records.dart`
is already 1024, and `PLAN.md`'s standing exclusion is that a further declaration makes the
existing drift worse.

### `motion.routeParallax`, the one new token

§6.2 states 30% and `claude.md` hard rule 2 forbids a widget restating it, so it joins
`pressScale` on `AppMotion` - the same kind of value, from the same section, in the same place.
`AppMotion.lerp` interpolates it and `tokens_test.dart` pins it.

### Reduced motion is a simulation, not a shorter duration

§2.4: "springs collapse to instant, durations to 0". `_InstantSimulation` is already at its end
and already done, so both rows collapse. The two alternatives were rejected for reasons worth
keeping: `transitionDuration = Duration.zero` is unreachable, because the duration is a getter
with no context and whether motion is disabled is a property of the surface; and
`AnimationController`'s own handling scales durations by 0.05 off
`SemanticsBinding.instance.disableAnimations`, which is a different flag from the one §2.4 names,
is invisible to a widget test that sets `MediaQueryData.disableAnimations`, and is a scale rather
than a collapse.

### Reading `MediaQuery` from a route without depending on it

The route resolves its row and its reduced-motion flag from the `MediaQuery` above the navigator,
through `context.getInheritedWidgetOfExactType<MediaQuery>()` rather than `MediaQuery.of`. A route
is not a widget and the context it has is the **navigator's**, so `MediaQuery.of` there would
rebuild the navigator - and therefore consider every route in it - on every metrics change, the
keyboard opening included.

The row is latched in `install()` and held for the life of the route. A transition that changed
identity half way through because a window was resized would be worse than either row.

### Three screenshots that are deliberately of a frame timeline

Every other capture in the harness is of a settled frame. A route transition has no settled state
to photograph - at rest it is just the screen that arrived - so `91-route-push-compact`,
`91-route-push-expanded` and `91-route-pop-compact` stop the clock 90ms in. `PLAN.md` records
`31b-a-receipt-found` as a hazard for exactly this shape, where it is an accident; here it is the
subject, and the pump budget is part of the specification of the picture. Two runs of identical
code still hash identically, so they stay attributable.

## One field, everywhere - 2026-08-12

`design.md` §11 step 3's second half, and with it **step 3 is finished**. `AppTextField` and
`AppSelect` are built to §5.2, and **39 call sites across 17 files** are them: 34 fields and 5
selects. Three Material fields remain in the migrated tree and all three are deliberate -
`checkout_cart_panel.dart`'s two are step 7's sale path, and `pill_input.dart`'s one is step 9's
sign-in.

### The audit was wrong about `AppSelect`, and the decision made on it had to be unmade

`DESIGN-AUDIT.md` §2.2 said flatly: "**There is no `DropdownButtonFormField` in the migrated
tree.**" The product owner, reading that, dropped `AppSelect` from §5.1 at the start of this
session. **There are five**, in `audit_log_panel`, `stock_adjustment_panel`,
`stock_movement_feed_panel`, `tenant_staff_invitation` and `tenant_staff_update` - which is exactly
the row §5.1 wrote for it.

The audit had looked at the two places a *category* is chosen, found `ChoiceChip` there, and
generalised from two call sites to a whole tree. The decision was put back to the product owner
with the real figure and reversed inside the same session, which is the only reason this cost
nothing: **a decision taken on a false premise is not a decision, and the cheapest moment to say so
is before building around it.** Both claims in `DESIGN-AUDIT.md` are struck through with the
correction rather than deleted.

### §5.2's rules that turn out to have layout consequences

**The error replaces the helper line; it does not join it.** One slot under the field holds one or
the other, so a field does not grow when it goes wrong - and a form does not reflow under the
finger typing into it. Asserted as a size equality rather than described.

**The counter renders only above 80% of the limit**, and counts *characters* rather than code
units, because that is the unit `maxLength` enforces. A counter that disagreed with the limit it
names would be worse than none. `TextField`'s own counter is suppressed rather than restyled: two
counters is worse than the wrong one.

**The label is above the field and always there.** This app broke that three different ways -
floating labels in the migrated tree, a placeholder standing in for a label, and uppercase labels
on sign-in - and the third is still there because §4.4 is step 9's.

### The focus ring re-parented the field and ate every keystroke

**The best bug of the session, and the second one this week with the same shape.** `PressSurface`
inserts its `Stack` when the control takes focus, which is harmless for a button. Doing the same in
a field changed the shape of the widget tree above its `TextField` the instant it was focused, so
the `TextField` was re-parented, its `EditableText` state went with it, and the platform input
connection dropped. **The field took focus and then refused every keystroke.**

It was found by a test that could not type into it, and the symptom was thoroughly misleading:
seven unrelated assertions failed - `onChanged` never firing, `maxLength` not enforcing, a
placeholder that would not go away - and none of them named focus. The fix is that the `Stack` is
always in the tree and the ring appears by *gaining a border* rather than by being inserted.

This is the same mechanism the route chunk hit six hours earlier from the other end, where a
shape change above a page re-parented it through a `GlobalKey` and cost a Firestore read. Recorded
as a standing trap in its general form: **changing the shape of the tree above a stateful subtree
is not free, and the cost does not look like the cause.**

### Finding 4, closed by moving a picker rather than adding one

The add-product form asked for a category and offered no way to choose one; the picker was the
chip row a screenful above, under the "Categories" heading that also serves as the list of
categories. The `Correct` dialog has always had an inline picker, so one screen did it both ways.

**The picker moved into the form, keeping its keys and its callback**, and the row under
"Categories" became what that heading says it is - a list, in plain `Chip`s. Nothing about what a
tap does changed, which is why this fits inside a visual chunk; the existing tests that tap
`catalog-management-category-cat-bakery` to select were not touched.

### `AppSelect` has no specification, and that is recorded rather than invented

§5.1 gives it a row; §5.2 specifies only the "load-bearing five", which it is not among. So it is
drawn as `AppTextField`'s chrome around a menu - the same label, well, border, radius, height,
helper and error - because "one pattern, everywhere" is §5.2's own first line and a second field
shape would contradict it. The only value not read straight from a §2 row is the menu's corner:
§2.3 names four radii and a menu is not among the things any of them lists, so `radius.md` is
applied as the nearest row rather than a fifth radius being invented.

### `hover` is in the harness showing nothing, on purpose

§5's matrix asks for every state that applies, and `hover` applies to a field on a pointer device.
**§5.2 specifies no hover treatment for one**, and `claude.md` forbids inventing a token, so
`92-appfield-hover` is a picture of no change at all. It is captured rather than omitted so a
reviewer can see the absence is deliberate: `90-appbutton-hover-*` shows a real change and this
shows none. Queued in `PLAN.md` as a question for the product owner.

`pressed` and `loading` are absent for the same reason `AppButton` has no `error`: a field is not a
control you push, and a field whose value is not ready is `disabled` or `read-only`, both of which
are in the matrix already.

## Five statuses, two notices, and prose that folds away - 2026-08-12

`design.md` §11 **step 4**: `StatusBadge`, `Callout` and `Disclosure`, built to §5.2 and §5.1, with
their state matrices in the harness and a first set of call sites on four real screens.

**This is the first quarter of the batched composition layer, not the whole batch.** The product
owner's 2026-08-12 exception lets steps 4, 5a, 6 and 8 ship as one chunk, and `PLAN.md` orders 4
first because `StatusBadge` is used by 6 and 8. Step 4 is what fitted this session; 5a, 6 and 8
stay batched and stay next. The exception is a permission to batch, not an instruction to, and
splitting on the boundary it names first costs the batch nothing.

### The web callable-auth defect was considered first, and could not be settled here

`PLAN.md`'s queued chunk explicitly told this session to think before inheriting the product
owner's choice: if the "callables arrive with auth missing" defect reproduces off web, the app is
broken past login for everyone and outranks any reskin step. **Settling it needs a device run, and
both routes to one are still shut** - `flutter run -d windows` needs Developer Mode, which is a
machine setting nobody should flip on the owner's behalf, and Android needs the emulators not to be
serving another session. Reading the source settles nothing either: every callable goes through
`FirebaseFunctions.instance` with no platform branch anywhere, so the client code is identical on
all three surfaces and the difference, if there is one, is in the emulator transport. So the
product owner's choice stands, and the open variable is recorded as still open rather than quietly
resolved.

### `ConfirmDialog` left step 4, and the answer was already written down

`PLAN.md` required this decided before starting. `DESIGN-AUDIT.md` §4.3 had the argument - it
consolidates four `await`-and-branch call sites, so it cannot ship as a visual change - but not the
destination. **§11 step 7's own row already says "destructive confirm"**, so it has a home in the
step that is already scoped as touching control flow. Nothing else in step 4 depended on it. The
decision is recorded inline in `DESIGN-AUDIT.md` §4.3.

### What each component decided, and what it refused to decide

**Only one of the three is specified in §5.2.** `Disclosure` has a paragraph and `StatusBadge` a
one-line row; `Callout` has a §5.1 row saying it replaces "permanent notice paragraphs" and no
measurements at all. It is therefore drawn the way `AppSelect` was in step 3 - out of §2 rows that
already exist, each named in the class doc comment - rather than out of taste.

**The glyphs are the component's and that is stated rather than smuggled.** §5.2 makes the icon
mandatory on a status and names no glyph for any of the five. Leaving it to each call site would
reproduce, in glyphs, exactly the one-green-for-seven-jobs drift §1 is about, so `AppStatus`
carries a default per status and a call site may override it. An icon is not a token - not a
colour, size, radius, spacing, duration or spring - which is why this is a decision rather than an
invention `claude.md` forbids.

**Two values §5.2 does not define were borrowed rather than invented**, and both are recorded in
`PLAN.md` as questions: `Disclosure`'s info glyph and chevron, and `Callout`'s leading glyph, all
take §5.2's *only* named leading-icon size, `AppButton`'s 18. The nearest-named-row precedent is
`AppSelect`'s menu radius from step 3.

**The status border question is closed in the token layer too.** `AppStatusRole`'s doc comment
still said the §2.1-vs-§9 border contrast was an unresolved conflict recorded in `PLAN.md`. It was
answered on 2026-08-12 and `design.md` §9 carries the sentence; the stale half is struck through in
place.

### Closed means gone from the tree, and the epsilon is the physics rather than a fudge

A collapsed `Disclosure` renders no part of its explanation, so a screen reader does not read out
prose nobody can see. Deciding *when* closed has arrived is the interesting part:
`SpringSimulation` finishes against `Tolerance`, whose defaults are absolute, so a spring asked for
zero parks within `1e-3` of it and stays there. Keying the removal on `extent == 0` left the prose
mounted forever after every close - which is how it was found, by a test that closed it and still
saw it. The condition is the widget's own flag **and**
`extent <= Tolerance.defaultTolerance.distance`, which asks the physics where "arrived" is instead
of guessing at it.

`SettlingSpringSimulation` in `lib/ui/spring.dart` is the other way to solve this and was
deliberately not wired into `SpringDrive`: that would change every press spring in the app for an
invisible difference, which is a wider blast radius than one component's reveal needs.

### The reveal is a spring, and the chevron rides the same one

§2.4 makes anything spatial a spring, and §2.4's own table names "expansion" under `spring.smooth`.
`AnimatedCrossFade` and `ExpansionTile` are both a duration and a curve, so neither was usable.
The chevron rotates off the same `SpringDrive` rather than off a second animation that could
disagree with it mid-flight. Two tests carry the claim: one that the reveal is between its ends one
frame in, and one that a second tap mid-flight moves it less than 4px in the next frame rather than
jumping to a mirrored position.

### Semantics: two labels that merged into one sentence twice

`Semantics(label: summary, child: PressSurface(child: Text(summary)))` announces "How a correction
reaches many products\nHow a correction reaches many products". The two labels merge into one node.
The header sets `button`, `expanded` and `enabled` and **no label**, letting the `Text` supply it.
Found by the semantics test, which is the only kind of test that could have.

### Call sites: four screens, and one status left deliberately alone

- **`tenant_staff_directory.dart`** - membership standing and invitation standing are `StatusBadge`
  now. Standing used to be a chip coloured `colors.error` or nothing. **Inactive is `neutral`, not
  `problem`**: §2.1 gives "closed" to neutral, and a deactivated member is closed rather than a
  difference found. **The role chip is deliberately still a `TenantStatusChip`** - a role is not one
  of the five statuses and dressing it as one is the failure this step exists to fix. It belongs to
  `FilterChipBar`, §5.1 priority 2.
- **`reconciliation_status_panel.dart`** - a badge above the verdict sentence, the manager notice as
  a `Callout`, and both long explanations as `Disclosure`s. The sentence stays beside the badge
  because it names *why*, which no five-word status can.
- **`catalog_management_panel.dart`** and **`stock_adjustment_panel.dart`** - the two paragraphs
  §5.2 names **by name** as prose to keep and fold away. The words are unchanged; only the summary
  line above each is new, and it is new because the component requires one.

**`reconciliation-request-notice` was left as a `Text` on purpose.** It is a `String?` the panel
passes down, and nothing in the model says whether a given notice is a success or a refusal.
Choosing a status by inspecting the sentence would be the guesswork this step is here to remove,
and making the parent pass a status is a change to what the parent computes - not a visual change.
Queued in `PLAN.md`.

**`unrecognised` is `info`, not `problem`.** §2.1 gives "unreadable" to `problem`, which looks like
the obvious home. But the existing comment on `_verdict` had already decided the opposite question
in words - a server state this app does not model is not evidence of anything wrong - and painting
it red would be inventing in colour an answer the code refuses to invent in prose.

## A screen title stops being chrome - 2026-08-12

`design.md` §11 **step 5a**: `AppScaffold` and `PageHeader`, per `DESIGN-AUDIT.md` §6 decision 3's
split of step 5. Every route in the migrated tree now sits in the same frame, with its title in the
page instead of in the toolbar. **5b, §4.4's navigation model, is not in this and stays queued** -
it is a behaviour change and needs a device check.

**This is the second quarter of the batched composition layer, not the whole batch.** The product
owner's 2026-08-12 exception lets steps 4, 5a, 6 and 8 ship as one chunk; `PLAN.md` orders 5a second
because 6 and 8 both sit inside the page frame. 5a is what fitted this session. The exception is a
permission to batch, not an instruction to, and splitting on the boundary it names has now cost the
batch nothing twice.

### The web callable-auth defect was checked again, and this time one half of it was measured

`PLAN.md` tells every session to think before inheriting the product owner's choice: if "callables
arrive with auth missing" reproduces off web, the app is broken past login for everyone and outranks
any reskin step. **The Windows route was checked rather than restated.**
`HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\AppModelUnlock` carries no
`AllowDevelopmentWithoutDevLicense` value at all, so Developer Mode is off and `flutter run -d
windows` still cannot link its plugins - a machine setting nobody should flip on the owner's behalf.
Android still needs the emulators not to be serving another session, and this session was using
them. The source settles nothing either, for the reason step 4 recorded. So the choice stands and
the variable is recorded as still open.

### What the frame decided

**The title left the toolbar because §2.2 will not fit in one.** `display` is 32 / 40 at weight 700
and no 56-high Material toolbar holds it. That is not a detail: it means `design.md` treats a screen
title as a piece of *content*, which is also what §7 means by "Title appears once" and by putting
`PageHeader` at the head of the page pattern rather than above it. So the title is in the page, at
`title.lg` below §4.1's `expanded` floor and `display` at or above it, and the toolbar keeps the way
back and the app-level actions that were already sitting beside it.

**`AppBar` was kept rather than hand-drawn.** It owns the leading control and the "is there a way
back from here" logic, the safe-area inset, the scrolled-under treatment and the toolbar semantics.
Redrawing it would have moved routing behaviour into a visual change, which `claude.md` hard rule 1
forbids. The title's `header: true` semantics moved with the title, because an `AppBar.title`
announced itself as a heading and losing that would have been a silent accessibility regression in
the one change whose whole subject is the title.

**The frame costs a route 72 logical pixels of body, and that is written down rather than
discovered.** A toolbar *and* a header where there used to be a toolbar: about 128 pixels of frame
on a 411 x 891 phone instead of 56. It buys §7's page pattern and §2.2's title roles. Whether it
reads as generous or as a near-empty strip above a title is a judgement no screenshot settles, and
it is now the **first** item on the device-run list, ahead of the field.

**Below 768 the primary action drops under the title instead of beside it, and that was found by a
test rather than reasoned out.** Laid side by side at phone width, a `Row` hands an unflexed action
all the width it asks for: with a product-name title and a five-word button label the title was
squeezed to a **two-pixel** column of wrapped letters, 1,596 pixels tall, overflowing its column by
896. §5.2's "never truncated" is about a title staying readable, and that fails it more completely
than an ellipsis would. The boundary is `tenantWideLayoutBreakpoint`, whose own doc comment says it
answers "is there room for two things side by side" - **it had zero consumers and now has one**.
`DESIGN-AUDIT.md` §5 is struck through in place; its reader `tenantLayoutIsWide` is still dead code,
because the header reads the constant against a screen width rather than against `BoxConstraints`.

**The title role is resolved against the screen, not the header's own box.** First written as a
`LayoutBuilder`, which failed its own test at exactly 1024: the box is the page inset narrower, so
`display` would have switched on at 1064 - a fourth breakpoint produced by arithmetic that nobody
declared and nobody could look up.

**The tab strip on the platform route moved out of `AppBar.bottom` and under the header.** §7's
order is *header -> callout -> filters -> content*, and a tab strip is this page's filter row;
leaving it in the toolbar would have put it above the title it filters. The `DefaultTabController`
still owns the selection.

**One screen had to change shape to pay for the frame, and it is the only one.** The business
selector laid its two transient panels - verify your address, request a business - at their natural
height above an `Expanded` list. At 800 x 600 with the request form open, the new header left 16
pixels too few and the form overflowed. They are a scrollable `Flexible` now. **It is an improvement
rather than a concession**: at the height where it first broke, the old layout had already crushed
the membership list to 56 pixels to make room for the form.

**`subtitle` and `primaryAction` ship with no call site, and that is stated rather than left to be
noticed.** Every migrated route kept its title verbatim: turning a title into a title-and-subtitle
pair is a copy decision and §11 step 11 is the copy pass, and hoisting a panel's primary action into
the frame crosses the screen/panel boundary that keeps these routes widget-testable. Both slots are
exercised by the harness and by `test/ui/scaffold_test.dart`.

### What it refused to decide

**§3's density.** `lib/ui/tokens.dart` has carried this since step 1 and `AppScaffold` is the widget
that would resolve it - the only thing every route has in common. It resolves nothing, because §3's
rule is a width test **and** an input test - *"a touch device never gets 32px targets whatever its
width"* - and Flutter has no honest answer to the second. `defaultTargetPlatform` describes the OS,
not the hardware: a Windows tablet, a Chromebook in tablet mode and a touchscreen desktop till are
all pointer platforms with fingers on them, and this app is for a shop counter.
`MouseTracker.mouseIsConnected` answers only after a mouse has moved. Picking one and calling it the
rule would put a 32 x 32 tap target on a real till, which is the one thing §9 makes pass/fail. Every
screen therefore stays comfortable, the stricter setting on every dimension §9 measures. Recorded in
`PLAN.md` as a question for the product owner; step 6 and step 8 will both want the answer.

**A page padding.** No section of `design.md` states one. `AppScaffold` uses `space.20`, which is on
§2.3's scale and is what the three largest list screens already pad their bodies with. Two routes
pad 24 and are 4 pixels out until step 6 unifies them; recorded rather than fixed, because fixing it
means editing bodies in a chunk about frames.

**Content widths.** §4.2's 720 / 1200 / 420 are step 6's, together with §4.1's rename. The seam is
now one widget instead of twenty-three.

## Every page gets a maximum width, and 768 stops being declared three times - 2026-08-12

`design.md` §11 **step 6, first half**: §4.1's breakpoints and §4.2's content widths. Every route in
the migrated tree now declares which of §4.2's rows it is, and the app has **one** declaration of
each layout boundary where it had four.

**Step 6 is split, and this is the half `PLAN.md` said to take on its own if it filled a session.**
§11 names step 6 "`RecordList` contract and content widths", which is two halves with a conjunction
between them. `DESIGN-AUDIT.md` §4.7 is explicit that the first half is not a rename of what exists
- it requires inventing the record model §5.2 describes, re-expressing thirteen screens' data in it,
and deciding per screen what the compact form loses, which is a product judgement per screen. So the
*contract* half is its own chunk and this one took the *widths* half, which is the one the
breakpoint rewiring belongs to. That is the shape `AppButton` and `AppTextField` both shipped in:
the mechanism first, the per-screen judgement second.

### The chunk was checked against the board before it was accepted

`prompt.md` asks a session to check the queued chunk rather than inherit it, and to propose
something else if a capability the app needs in order to function is missing and unqueued. Nothing
is: password reset is blocked on the App Check decision and queued, the printed receipt is blocked
on an external interface, and the subscription has no schema to model. The queued chunk stands.

### The web callable-auth defect was checked again, and the Windows route is still shut

`HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\AppModelUnlock` still carries no
`AllowDevelopmentWithoutDevLicense` value, so Developer Mode is off and `flutter run -d windows`
cannot link its plugins. The source settles nothing, for the reason step 4 recorded: every callable
goes through `FirebaseFunctions.instance` with no platform branch anywhere. **The variable is still
open** and the next session inherits the same instruction rather than a resolved one.

### What the layout contract decided

**One declaration, and it absorbed a mechanism the audit did not count at first.**
`DESIGN-AUDIT.md` §5 named `tenantWideLayoutBreakpoint` (768), `tenantTableBreakpoint` (1024) and
`checkout_cart_panel.dart`'s `wideTillBreakpoint` (768 again), and then found a third mechanism:
`login_screen.dart` computing `width < 768` inline with a comment. All four are gone. `AppLayout` in
`lib/ui/tokens.dart` holds §4.1's two floors and §4.2's three widths, and every former caller reads
it. **The numbers did not move**, which §4.1 asks for in so many words - a rename that moved a
figure would be a layout change wearing a rename's clothes - and `test/ui/tokens_test.dart` asserts
both floors as literals so it cannot happen quietly.

**Two of the four declarations were in files this chunk is otherwise forbidden to touch, and that is
sanctioned rather than smuggled.** `checkout_cart_panel.dart` is step 7's sale path and
`login_screen.dart` is step 9's sign-in. §4.1 names both files as part of its own rewiring, and
`PLAN.md`'s queued chunk says in as many words that "step 6 is where they become one name". Each
edit is one expression - a constant becomes a getter, an inline comparison becomes a call - neither
file's visual design was touched, and neither file's screenshots moved.

**A band is resolved from a screen width, never from a `BoxConstraints`.** §4.1 states its ranges as
properties of the surface a person is looking at. `PageHeader` already made this argument for the
title role in step 5a; step 6 made it load-bearing, because §4.2 now puts a 1200 cap and 20 of
padding between the screen and any widget inside it. The one place in the app that switched layout
on a `BoxConstraints` - the staff directory's card-to-table switch, which `DESIGN-AUDIT.md` §5 calls
the only breakpoint-driven switch in the migrated app - was moved to the screen width for exactly
that reason: at 1024 the old reading would have found 984 and drawn cards on a surface §4.1 calls
expanded. **Neither screenshot viewport is near that boundary, so it moved no image**, which is what
made it safe to do inside a chunk about widths.

**`AppScaffold.contentWidth` is required, and it is the decision here most likely to be argued
with.** §4.2 opens "Every screen has a max content width" and gives a form and a table different
ones, so there is no value that is right when a call site says nothing. A default would also have
been silently wrong for the majority: **20 of the 25 routes are record lists**, so defaulting to
`reading` would have quietly narrowed most of the app to 720 and defaulting to `records` would have
quietly widened every form to 1200. Requiring it puts the judgement in the diff, one line per
screen, where a reviewer can disagree with it per screen. The five reading surfaces are checkout
settings, receipt lookup, one reconciliation run, and the shell's two invitation screens.

**The header and the body are constrained together; the toolbar is not.** A title at the window edge
above records in a centred column would read as two pages rather than one, and constraining the
shared column is also what keeps the header's 20 inset lined up with the 20 every body pads itself
with. The toolbar is deliberately outside: a back arrow that drifted inwards on a wide window, away
from the corner every platform puts it in, would be chrome obeying a content rule.

**`AppContentWidth.full` adds no widget rather than an unbounded one.** `maxWidthOf` answers null
there, so the `ConstrainedBox` is not built at all - a box that constrains nothing is a line that
has to be read before it can be ignored. Nothing in `lib/` passes `full` yet; the sale would, and it
is step 7's. It is built, tested and photographed anyway, because §4.2 states the row and a sale
screen that quietly got 1200 would be missing 240 pixels of products.

**The three routes that padded 24 now pad 20**, which is the unification step 5a recorded as owed
rather than a new opinion. Checkout settings and the shell's two invitation screens were four pixels
out from their own headers. The figure did not change; three bodies moved to it.

**Nothing overrides the layout contract per subtree, unlike density.** §3 says outright that density
is "chosen by the screen"; §4.1 and §4.2 state ranges and maxima no screen is entitled to disagree
with. It still lives on `AppTokens` rather than as a bare top-level constant, for the same reason
`AppSpacing` does, and `tokens_test` asserts the registered set carries `AppLayout.contract` itself -
which is what lets `PageHeader`'s two statics read the constant where they have no context to read a
theme from.

### What it did not do

- **The `RecordList` contract**, the other half of step 6 and the larger one. §4.3 is untouched, and
  `DESIGN-AUDIT.md` §6 decision 2 - amending §4.3 to concede the caller's opt-out - is still
  unapplied to `design.md`, because it belongs with the half that implements §4.3.
- **The step-4 sweep** and **step 8**, both still in the batch and both queued.
- **§3's density**, still unresolved and still owed by `AppScaffold`. Step 6's second half and step 8
  both want the answer.

### ~~The three emulator suites cannot start on this machine, and it is the toolchain~~ — false, retracted 2026-08-13

**Every claim in this section is wrong, and the error message quoted below is the only true thing in
it.** The suites start. The machine has had a portable Temurin **21.0.12** at
`D:\firebase-emulator-tools\jdk21\jdk-21.0.12+8` since before this work began, and `PLAN.md`'s own
"The emulator prelude is not optional" section - together with **eleven** earlier entries in this
very file - gives the three lines that reach it. **This session ran `emulators:exec` bare.** With
the prelude, all three pass first time: 161, 10, 23, measured 2026-08-13.

The section is left standing rather than deleted because the failure it demonstrates is worth more
than the section: **it read an environment error as evidence about the environment, without using
the documented environment.** The chunk after it inherited the conclusion, repeated it, escalated it
to a blocking decision for the product owner, and searched `C:\Program Files` for a JDK 21 while
this file said it was on `D:`. **The product owner corrected it from memory.** See that session's
own entry for the full account.
