## A figure becomes a component, and the money screens stop writing numbers into sentences - 2026-08-14

`design.md` §11 **step 8, first half**: the money component, its existing call sites, and the two
money screens — the daily summary (25) and the period totals (26) — including the step-4 sweep of
their prose, which the catalog chunk decided the same day should travel *with* step 8 rather than
ahead of it.

```text
the component      lib/ui/stats.dart        StatTile, StatRow, StatLine
its old call sites 13 staff directory       TenantStatStrip -> StatRow
                   21 product stock         TenantStatCard  -> StatTile
step 8's screens   25 daily summary         figures, prose, and a day's standing
                   26 sales totals          figures, prose, tender split
still to come      27, 28, 29               already swept for step 4; their figures are next
```

It changes `firestore.rules` not at all and nothing in `functions/` or `rules-tests/` either:
`git diff` **and** `git status` over all three print zero lines. **It changed no status board row**,
and that is stated rather than left silent: "Read daily and period totals" and "See profit or
margin" have both been 🟢 throughout, and a shop can read exactly what it could read this morning.

### Why this chunk, and why it stops where it does

`PLAN.md` queued step 8 and named the pairing. Checking it against the board first: every red row is
either blocked on a decision nobody has made (App Check, the printer interface) or deliberately
sequenced after the first deployment (suspicious-return scoring), so nothing the app needs in order
to function is missing and unqueued, and the queued chunk stands.

**Step 8 is three things — `StatTile`, tabular figures, tables — and the third is already built.**
Tables are `RecordList`'s `RecordForm.table`, which step 6 shipped and which the reporting screens
already reach. So what step 8 actually owes is the component and the figures, and this chunk takes
the component plus the two screens that are *only* figures. 27, 28 and 29 keep their prose from the
reconciliation sweep and want their figures restyled, which is the next chunk.

### What was decided

1. **The three widgets, and which of them §5.1 actually names.** `StatTile` is §5.1's own row,
   replacing the "recorded stock" / "ledger entries" tiles by name. `StatRow` is the name §7 uses in
   passing — "the checkout queue counts belong in a `StatRow`" — and has no row of its own.
   **`StatLine` is in neither section**, and that is stated in its own doc comment rather than
   smuggled, the way `RecordItem.details` was in step 6: it is one label and one figure on a line,
   for money *in flow*, and it exists because two reporting surfaces render exactly that shape.
2. **A stat tile is for the one figure a surface exists for; a list of days is not that.** §2.2 gives
   `numeric.hero` exactly one use in the whole document — "the one figure a stat tile exists for" —
   and `numeric.body` the row "money and counts in flow". So screen 26, which answers one question
   with one pair of figures, gets tiles; screen 25, which lists seven days, gets `StatLine`s. The
   alternative was three hero tiles per day, which on a phone is a summary two and a half times
   taller than the sentences it replaces.
3. **The minimum tile width is measured, not chosen.** `TenantStatStrip` carried `minimumWidth = 168`
   — a number `design.md` does not contain, set when every figure in this app was two or three
   digits. `numeric.hero` is 28px at weight 700, so `KES 3810.25` is about 190 logical pixels of
   glyphs before the tile's own padding, and at 411 that strip would have put two money tiles side by
   side and ellipsised both. `StatRow.minimumTileWidth` lays every figure out with a `TextPainter` at
   `numeric.hero` and takes the widest plus the tile's own padding. **No constant, no caller knob, and
   no figure truncated** — and it is font-independent, which is what makes it assertable in a plain
   `flutter test` where the fallback face's advance widths are not Roboto's.
4. **The caption stopped being uppercase, which closes the last one in `lib/`.** §2.2 permits
   uppercase on `label.eyebrow` only, and permits `label.eyebrow` on "field group labels only" — both
   halves point away from a stat caption, so it is `label.md` in the case the caller wrote.
   `lib/ui/tokens.dart` named this component as the one uppercase surface left, and that note is now
   retracted at the text. `label.eyebrow`'s only readers are the harness's own section headings.
5. **An `emphasis` colour became a `StatusBadge`, and only where nothing else states the standing.**
   `TenantStatCard.emphasis` painted the figure red for a negative stock count, which is §9's "out of
   stock signalled by red text alone" in another place. Screen 21's tile carries `problem` / `Below
   zero` now — a container, a glyph and a word. **The staff directory's `Pending` tile carries
   nothing**, and that asymmetry is the decision: every pending member in the list below already
   wears an `attention` badge, so a second one on the *count* of them is the same signal twice. A
   count is a fact; the standing belongs to the records. Its old emphasis was `onSurfaceVariant`,
   which was a dimming that meant "look here" — exactly §2.1's complaint — so it goes rather than
   being converted.
6. **A day's standing is a §2.1 lookup and it was a sentence.** "Not reconciled yet." is
   `attention`'s stated meaning — *"unreconciled, pending, awaiting"* — and a reconciled day is
   `ok`'s, *"reconciled, confirmed"*, word for word. Both are badges now, on the day's own header
   row. It passes the every-row test: today is `attention` and the days behind it are `ok`, so the
   badge carries signal down the list rather than decorating every card.
7. **The profit statement's sentence became two figures, and its note did not fold.** "Profit: KES
   430.25, a margin of 34.4%." put two figures inside one sentence at whatever weight the surrounding
   body text happened to be. They are `StatLine`s now, both at `numeric.body`, both aligned to the
   same right edge. **The note stays directly under them as visible caption text**: the whole point
   of that widget is that no profit figure is rendered without, in the same block, what is known
   about the cost data behind it, and a `Disclosure` would make the qualification optional to read.
8. **The tender disclaimer is the family's one `Callout` among folds.** Every other permanent
   explanation on screen 26 went behind a `Disclosure` — the page's own basis, and the two
   explanations of the odd buckets, each true of its row every time that row appears. The disclaimer
   may not, because `checkout_tender.dart` requires *every* surface showing a tender to say the
   payment is unverified, and a sentence behind a chevron is one a person can finish the screen
   without reading. §2.1's `info` is "informational" in its own words.
9. **A failed read became a `problem` `Callout` with its retry inside it.** §2.1 gives `problem` the
   meaning "difference found, unreadable", and a read that produced no figure is unreadable. The
   action stays the caller's `AppButton` in `Callout.action`; the component decides where it sits and
   nothing about what it does.
10. **A row of tiles is rows, not a `Wrap`.** The first pictures showed a badge-carrying tile
    standing taller than the plain one beside it, which reads as an unfinished layout rather than as
    a difference that means anything. `IntrinsicHeight` per run is cheap at four tiles and is the
    only honest way to say "as tall as the tallest of you".

### §7 says "Title appears once", and thirteen more screens say it twice

**Both money screens drew their own `headlineSmall` copy of the title under the `PageHeader` that
already carries one.** That is the defect §7 names in its own words — "Today several screens render
the title in the app bar *and* again as an `H1` directly beneath it" — and step 5a moved the title
into the header without removing the copies underneath. Both are gone here, and the tests assert it
by construction: they pump the panel *without* its screen, so a title found in the panel is a second
one.

**It is not two screens.** `grep -n headlineSmall lib` finds the same shape in thirteen more panels,
including several the sweep has already been through: `audit_log_panel.dart`,
`sale_history_panel.dart` (twice), `receipt_lookup_panel.dart`, `return_history_panel.dart`,
`stock_product_ledger_panel.dart`, `shift_history_panel.dart`, `reconciliation_run_panel.dart`,
`stock_movement_feed_panel.dart`, `reconciliation_anomalies_panel.dart`,
`reconciliation_status_panel.dart`, `stock_adjustment_panel.dart`, `stock_adjustment_feed_panel.dart`
and `shift_amendment_feed_panel.dart`. `web/21-product-stock` shows it plainly: **White bread loaf**

## A difference states its figures, and step 8 is finished - 2026-08-15

`design.md` §11 **step 8, second half**, which finishes step 8: the figures on the three
reconciliation surfaces — the day page (27), the unresolved differences list (28) and the one-run
page (29). All three had already been swept for step 4 on 2026-08-14, so this chunk inherited no
prose work and is only what step 8 is about.

```text
27 reconciliation status   StatTile x2 on the day card, StatLines in every run card
28 unresolved differences  StatLines per difference, and a second rendering of one document
29 one reconciliation run  the shared run card's counts; no tile row, deliberately
shared                     lib/reporting/reconciliation_labels.dart gains the figure model
```

It changes `firestore.rules` not at all and nothing in `functions/` or `rules-tests/` either:
`git diff` **and** `git status` over all three print zero lines. **It changed no capability board
row**, and that is stated rather than left silent: "Ask for reconciliation", "See why a day
disagrees, and correct a shift" and "Adjust stock" have all been 🟢 throughout, and a shop can do
exactly what it could do yesterday. It moved the **Design system** track 85% to 88%.

### Why this chunk, and why it stops where it does

`PLAN.md` queued it. Checking that against the board first, as the instruction requires: every red
row is either blocked on a decision nobody has made (App Check for password reset, an external
interface for the printed receipt) or deliberately sequenced after the first deployment
(suspicious-return scoring), so nothing the app needs in order to function is missing and unqueued,
and the queued chunk stands.

It stops at the figures. The four notice-status model changes, the thirteen duplicate screen titles,
the four carried `RecordList` column observations, `Pagination`, and `RecordList` for screen 28's
difference cards were all excluded going in and all stayed excluded — see the exclusions below,
where the two that were *hardest* to leave are named.

### What was decided

1. **Screen 29 gets no `StatTile` row, and `PLAN.md` predicted one.** The prediction was reasonable:
   a run does have a small set of headline counts. It is wrong once the screen is open. Every one of
   those counts is already stated by `TenantReconciliationRunCard`, which 29 shares with 27 precisely
   so that two routes cannot describe one run differently, and a tile row above the card would print
   `Stock differences 1` at 28px and `Stock differences 1` at 14px a centimetre below it. That is
   step 8's own first-half finding — two adjacent things saying one figure — one level up. The
   figures went into the shared card, where both routes get them.
2. **One document is deliberately rendered two ways, and both live in one `switch`.** This is the
   chunk's real cost and it came from a screen *outside* the chunk. Screen 21's "Reconciliation
   found" section draws a difference as a `Callout`, and `Callout` takes a `message` string with no
   slot for a widget; screen 28 draws the same record as a card that can hold a column of figures. So
   the prose could not simply be replaced by figures. `reconciliation_labels.dart` now declares each
   kind's reading once, as a private `_DifferenceReading` holding the sentence, the prose left once
   the figures are pulled out, and the figures themselves — adjacent lines in one `switch` — and
   `reconciliation_labels_test.dart` asserts that every figure's magnitude also appears in that
   kind's sentence. **The obvious move was a second module**, and it would have re-created the exact
   divergence this module was written to end.
3. **A variance states its direction twice.** `Difference -3` with `fewer than the ledger accounts
   for` on the line under the label. A sign is a one-glyph signal; §9's rule that a status is never
   colour alone is the same rule. It also fixed something the sentence did badly: a shift variance of
   zero used to read "its transaction count agrees", a *word* where the other half of the same
   comparison was a number. It is `0` beside `agrees with the sales recorded` now.
4. **A revision is not a figure.** "The published totals were generated from change 2; the day has
   since reached change 3." stays prose. §2.2's numeric roles are for money and counts; a revision is
   a generation marker, nothing about it is worth comparing by magnitude, and promoting it would be
   applying the letter of step 8 against its own reason. It is the one number on these three screens
   deliberately left in a sentence, and it has an entry in `PLAN.md` against it.
5. **A figure label is a column heading and is never inflected.** `Unreadable sale lines: 1`. The
   prose form still says "1 sale line could not be read", because there it is a clause. Same grammar
   the daily summary deleted rather than guarded in step 8's first half.
6. **The three panels moved onto the token layer while they were open.** They were the last reporting
   surfaces reading `Theme.of(context).textTheme` and padding with bare integers — `claude.md` hard
   rule 2 — where 25 and 26 have been on tokens since the first half. **One `Theme.of` read survives
   in each file on purpose**: the in-body `headlineSmall` screen title, which is §7's queued
   thirteen-panel defect, and all three sites now carry a comment saying so rather than being
   silently left.

### Safety

**No behaviour changed.** No repository call, no callable payload, no routing condition, no state
shape, no new document read. The one structural change in `lib/` is that
`TenantReconciliationRunPanel`'s builder body became a private `_RunContents` widget so it could read
the token set — same tree, same keys, same loads.

**A capability was deliberately not added.** `TenantReconciliationRun` decodes `metricsProcessed`,
`productsProcessed` and `shiftsProcessed` — literally "what the run read and what it wrote", which is
what `PLAN.md` predicted these screens would want — and **no surface has ever displayed any of the
three**. Showing them is new content on a screen rather than a new rendering of existing content, so
it is recorded as an open decision rather than taken inside a visual chunk.

**A §8 rule was found half-broken and left that way, which is worth stating plainly.** §8 rule 8 says
money is always currency-coded. Screen 28 states a shift's sales variance as `-12.5` with no code,
and has since it was written — the sentence it replaced said "is 12.5 short" and carried no code
either. This chunk made it tabular and did not make it coded, because the code lives in
`configuration/checkout` and reading it is a repository call, which hard rule 1 forbids here. It is
an open decision in `PLAN.md` with three named resolutions, none of them a restyle.

## A notice says which answer it is, and four of them were never refusals - 2026-08-15

The notice-status model, queued by `PLAN.md` as four sites. **It was seven.** `lib/ui/status.dart`
gains `AppNotice`, and the seven surfaces that report what a write has just done stopped carrying a
`String?` whose meaning was in the sentence.

```text
27 reconciliation status   reconciliation-request-notice     queued
28 unresolved differences  reconciliation-amend-notice       queued
18 manage catalog          catalog-management-notice         queued
20 bulk changes/import     bulk-catalog-notice               queued
21 product stock           product-stock-notice              never listed
34 returns on a sale       sale-returns-notice               never listed
16 checkout settings       checkout-configuration-notice     never listed
14 the till                checkout-code-notice              step 7, excluded
```

It changes `firestore.rules` not at all and nothing in `functions/` or `rules-tests/` either. **It
changed no capability board row**: every capability these seven sit on — adding a category, correcting
a product, adjusting stock, recording and verifying a return, publishing a currency, asking for
reconciliation, correcting a shift — has been 🟢 throughout and does exactly what it did this morning.
It moved the **Design system** track 88% to 90%.

### Why this chunk, and why it stops where it does

`PLAN.md` queued it, and the reason it was at the head is that step 8's second half had both
reconciliation panels open earlier the same day and left both notices untouched for the second time.
An item deferred twice while its file is open is on its way to being permanent.

Checking it against the board first, as the instruction requires: every red row is blocked on a
decision nobody has made (App Check, the printer interface) or sequenced after the first deployment
(suspicious-return scoring). Nothing the app needs in order to function is missing and unqueued.

It stops at the model and the seven call sites. `checkout_cart_panel.dart`'s eighth notice is the sale
path and stays with step 7; the thirteen duplicate screen titles, the four `RecordList` column
observations and `Pagination` were excluded going in and stayed excluded.

### What was decided

1. **Four named constructors, not a status argument, and that is the whole design.**
   `AppNotice.confirmed / .refused / .unknown / .offline` are the four outcomes this app's write
   boundaries already answer in — `TenantCatalogWriteKind` is literally `committed / rejected /
   ambiguous / unavailable`, and every other gateway matches. Mapping them once, here, means a call
   site names *what happened* and never picks a colour. An `AppNotice(message, status)` at seventy
   call sites would have reproduced, in statuses, exactly the drift §1 describes in colours. The
   general constructor exists and is used **once**, in a test.
2. **There is deliberately no `neutral` constructor.** §2.1 gives `neutral` "archived, retired,
   closed", which is a standing a *record* has. A page reporting on a write it just attempted never
   has one, and its absence is what stops a call site reaching for it — the bulk report gives
   `neutral` to an unchanged *row*, and one status meaning two things at two scales is the failure
   §2.1 exists to end. A test asserts no constructor produces it.
3. **Four branches across the seven were never refusals, and this is the finding.**
   `TenantProductUpdateFailure.unchanged`, the catalog's `product_unchanged` code, checkout settings'
   `currency_unchanged`, and `TenantReturnVerificationFailure.alreadyVerified` all say the same
   thing: *what you asked for is already true*. Every one had been drawn in the same black paragraph,
   in the same position, as "Only an owner or administrator may change this". They are `info` now.
   The clearest is the return: a manager who verifies an already-verified return is told the stock is
   restored, not that something failed.
4. **Every `ambiguous` branch is `attention` rather than `problem`, and there are six.** Nothing is
   known to have failed, the write may well have landed, and each of those sentences already says
   where to look. Painting them red would report a failure the app has no evidence of — the same
   argument the reconciliation vocabulary makes for an unmodelled run state being `info` rather than
   "unreadable".
5. **`bulk-catalog-notice` has no success branch at all and carries an `AppNotice` anyway.** It is set
   from exactly one place, a refusal raised before anything is sent. The type states that invariant
   where a `String?` left it to be traced through the assignments.
6. **The amend notice's trail button became the `Callout`'s own action.** §5.1 gives that component an
   action slot for one control belonging to the notice, which is precisely what "View this shift's
   corrections" is — the row it names has been deleted from the list, or may have been.

### Safety

**No behaviour changed.** No repository call, no callable payload, no routing condition, no state
shape, no new read. `AppNotice` replaces a `String?` field on seven `State` classes and a `String?`
parameter on seven presentational widgets. Every branch that set a notice still sets one, with the
same words: the only sentence that changed anywhere is a re-wrap.

## A title appears once, and one page was telling everybody it was read-only - 2026-08-15

§7's "Title appears once", the defect `design.md` names in its own words: *"several screens render the
title in the app bar **and** again as an `H1` directly beneath it"*. Step 5a moved every screen title
into a `PageHeader` and left the in-body copies where they were. `grep -n headlineSmall lib` over the
migrated tree returns **two** live uses now, both deliberate and both commented at the site.

**`PLAN.md` queued thirteen panels. It was fourteen sites in fourteen files**:
`tenant_staff_directory.dart` was never on the list, and `sale_history_panel.dart` held two. That is
the fourth queued list this file has under-counted from memory in three days, and the entry now
carries the grep rather than the number.

It changes `firestore.rules` not at all and nothing in `functions/` or `rules-tests/`. **It changed no
capability board row.** It moved the **Design system** track 90% to 92%.

### Why this chunk, and why it stops where it does

`PLAN.md` queued it, and named the thing to settle first: whether `PageHeader.subtitle` gets
populated. Checking against the board first, as the instruction requires: every red row is blocked on
a decision nobody has made or sequenced after the first deployment, so nothing the app needs in order
to function is missing and unqueued.

### What was decided

1. **The rule was in `PageHeader.subtitle`'s own doc comment all along.** The slot exists for "where
   the screen needs to say which slice of something it is showing - a date, a product, a period", and
   was populated at no call site because step 5a ruled that *rewriting* a title into a
   title-and-subtitle pair is a copy decision for step 11. **Moving a string the screen already draws
   is not that.** So: a heading that says what the `AppScaffold` title says is deleted; a heading that
   names *which* record the route is showing becomes the subtitle.
2. **The noun goes with it.** `Reconciliation run` over `rj_000001` is what the header already says;
   `Run rj_000001` underneath repeats the noun directly above its own value, which is the same
   duplication one line smaller. Same for `Returns` over the receipt number and `Shift corrections`
   over the shift ID.
3. **The staff directory's heading was also stating something false, and nothing had ever asserted
   it.** `Read-only staff directory` was drawn **unconditionally**, under an `AppScaffold` titled
   `Staff directory`, on a page that then offered an owner `Invite staff` two lines below. A page's
   standing is §2.1's rather than a heading's. It is an `info` `Callout` now, shown only when the
   session can neither invite nor edit - both conditions the page's own affordances already ask. This
   is the repair the read-only catalog already carries, reached from the other direction: there the
   fact was true and stated twice; here it was stated once and true only sometimes.
4. **Screen 24's heading stays, and it is not a duplicate.** `Product stock ledger` and `White bread
   loaf` say different things, so it is a subtitle candidate rather than a deletion - and it cannot
   become one. `TenantProductLedgerScreen` is constructed with a `productId`; the *name* only exists
   after the guarded load inside the panel. Reaching it means an optional decoded product on the
   screen, which its callers - the movement feed included - do not all hold, or hoisting the load out
   of the guard. Both are structure rather than a title fix.
5. **The unscoped shift-corrections route carries no subtitle at all.** A page showing the whole
   business is not a slice of anything, so the slot stays empty rather than being filled with a word
   meaning "everything". A test asserts it is null.

## A table stops guessing how wide its columns are - 2026-08-15

The four observations `PLAN.md` had been carrying against `RecordList`'s table since step 6b, taken
as one chunk because they are one defect seen from four directions. Step 6b divided a table row with
four constants - identity 3, status 2, actions 3, an attribute 1 - measured against a **two-column
activity log**, and the twelve screens that followed carry **two to six** columns. A share is a guess
about content, and the content is in the list.

It changes `firestore.rules` not at all and nothing in `functions/` or `rules-tests/`. **It changed
no capability board row**, and it moved the **Design system** track 92% to 93%.

### Why this chunk, and why it stops where it does

`PLAN.md` queued it, and queued it as a chunk rather than as four items for a reason it stated: a
changed column share moves every one of the twelve migrated screens, so it needs all twelve in front
of it, and all twelve exist. Checking against the board first, as the instruction requires: every red
row is blocked on a decision nobody has made, a schema that does not exist, or a sequencing choice
after the first deployment, so nothing the app needs in order to function is missing and unqueued.

### What was decided

1. **Measure, do not retune.** The alternative `PLAN.md` named for three of the four was a caller
   knob - `RecordList(actionsFlex: …)` beside `RecordAttribute.flex`. It was declined because it
   answers the question twelve times: every screen would have to be looked at, tuned, and looked at
   again whenever its data changed, and the number a caller would type is a number it cannot know,
   since it depends on the other columns. `RecordTableColumns` asks each column what its own widest
   content needs and divides the row by the answers.
2. **The old constants survive as ceilings, and that is what makes this safe on twelve screens at
   once.** A column may claim up to its share and never more, so no column can starve its neighbours
   with one long value, and a table where every column wants at least its share lays out exactly as
   it did before. The first pass therefore always fits; the two passes after it hand out only what
   the first pass left over. **The allocation cannot overflow at any width**, which is asserted at
   five widths from 320 to 2400.
3. **The pool is levelled, not shared in proportion — the decision most worth arguing with.**
   Proportion is the obvious rule and it is wrong here: a column 6 pixels short and a column 400
   short are not two claims of the same kind, because satisfying the small one removes a wrapped line
   and part-satisfying the large one removes nothing. So the pool rises like water - every unmet
   column takes the same amount until it is satisfied and drops out, deepest need served last. The
   staff directory is exactly that shape, and it is what let `Role`, `Invitation` and the identity all
   be satisfied before the actions took the remainder.
4. **A title asks for half its width and everything else asks for all of its own.** §5.2 gives the
   identity two lines before it ellipsises, so a title demanding its one-line width would ask for
   twice what it is entitled to. The subtitle and the provenance line are `maxLines: 1` and ask for
   all of theirs, which is what closes observation 3.
5. **The leftover goes to the identity**, because something has to absorb it and §5.2's "never
   truncated below two lines" row is the one column where more room is always worth having. It is
   the only column that is ever given more than it asked for, and there is a test saying so.
6. **A component answers for its own geometry.** `StatusBadge.measureWidth` and
   `AppButton.measureWidth` are new, and the table asks them rather than reassembling §5.2's padding
   rules at the call site - which would have been a second copy of the specification, going stale on
   the first change to the first. Both are asserted against the width the widget actually lays out
   at, which is how the two corrections below were found.
7. **`space.12` between adjacent cells**, from §2.3's scale. `design.md` did not ask for a gutter and
   does now; it is the cheapest of the four repairs and the only one that costs width rather than
   saving it.

### Two corrections the measurement made to itself, both found by rendering rather than by review

**A button is wider than §5.2 says it is, twice over.** `PressSurface` reserves the focus ring's
`width + offset` on every side whether it is visible or not, and §9's tap target is a **minimum
width** as well as a minimum height. A formula that agreed with §5.2 and disagreed with the widget by
8 pixels a button is exactly enough to wrap the set of four it had just made room for.

**Every `Text` in this app is painted 0.25 pixels per character wider than the token style says.** A
style with `inherit: true` - every style in the token layer - is merged onto the enclosing
`DefaultTextStyle`, and this app's `ThemeData` carries Material's own `letterSpacing: 0.25` on the
roles §2.2 does not set one for. On a word it is nothing; on `Cancel invitation` it is 4.25 pixels,
and on a four-button set it is the difference between one line and two. Every measurement here takes
the ambient style as an argument. **The theme half of that is a finding rather than a repair** - see
`PLAN.md`, because correcting it would move every string in the app and is a §2.2 question.

### What the four observations actually cost, against what `PLAN.md` predicted

| | Observation | Outcome |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | four actions wrap to three runs | **Improved, not closed.** Three runs to two on the staff directory at 1440; one run wherever the row has slack, which the tests assert and `96-record-columns` shows it does not always have |
| 2 | the status column is a wide left margin | **Closed.** It is the widest badge in the list and nothing more |
| 3 | the identity wraps its provenance line | **Closed on `23-stock-movements`**, which is the screen it was observed on; still wrapped on `30-shift-corrections`, which is six columns and out of room |
| 4 | no gap between cells | **Closed everywhere** |

**Observation 1 is the one to argue with, and the arithmetic says it cannot be closed by arithmetic.**
Four actions with real labels need about 630 pixels. The staff directory's other four columns need
about 700 between them, and the row is 1128. Something has to wrap, and what this chunk changed is
*how much*: the pool now goes to the actions column after the small claims are met, rather than to
whichever column had the larger constant. Sizing the column to the widest set instead - the obvious
"intrinsic" answer - was rejected on the picture: four of the five rows have two actions, so the
column would be 380 pixels of nothing on 80% of the table.

### Safety

**No behaviour changed.** No repository call, no callable payload, no routing condition, no new read,
no state. `RecordList`'s public API is unchanged except for additions: `RecordTableColumns` is new and
exposed for tests, `RecordActionSet.measureWidth`, `AppButton.measureWidth`, `AppButton.iconSize` and
`StatusBadge.measureWidth` are new statics, and `RecordAttribute.flex` keeps its name and its call
sites while its meaning narrows from an allocation to a ceiling. **No call site changed at all**: the
twelve migrated screens are untouched, which is the point of the component owning its own form.

`AppButton` gained one line of behaviour-free tidying: the leading icon's `18` is now
`AppButton.iconSize`, read by the widget that paints it and by the formula that measures it, so the
two cannot disagree.

### Files changed

```text

lib/ui/buttons.dart          AppButton.iconSize, AppButton.measureWidth
lib/ui/status.dart           StatusBadge.measureWidth
lib/ui/record_list.dart      RecordTableColumns; RecordActionSet.measureWidth; the table and its
                             rows lay out against measured widths with a space.12 gutter
test/ui/record_list_test.dart  +14 (the arithmetic, the gutter, the row height, the invariant)
test/ui/buttons_test.dart      +3  (measurement against rendering, §9's floor, 200% text)
test/ui/status_test.dart       +1  (measurement against rendering)
tool/screenshots/record_list_test.dart  96-record-columns, at all three bands
design.md                    §4.3 records the rule; it specified no column widths at all

```

`dart format` was not run, on any file, per the standing prohibition.

**All five suites measured, none carried.** Twelve consecutive chunks measuring all five.

**Every one of the 26 is `web/` or `web-full/`**, which is the check rather than an aside: the table

outright. Recorded here because a defect that is seen, understood, and deliberately not fixed looks
identical in a log to one nobody noticed, and only one of those is a decision. Fixing it at the theme
was offered and is the wrong repair: `inputDecorationTheme` is what the till's fields correctly read.

## The front door stops having a palette of its own - 2026-08-15

### Why this chunk, and why it stops where it does

`design.md` §11 step **9**, sign-in. It was the queued chunk, it is the next numbered step that is
neither excluded (7, the sale path) nor a behaviour change (5b, the navigation model), and
everything ahead of it closed earlier the same day. Nothing red on the capability board is both
required-to-function and unqueued: password reset is blocked on an App Check decision, printing on
an external interface, subscription has no schema, and suspicious-return scoring is sequenced after
the first deployment.

**It was one screen rather than the eight §11 lists, and both of this repository's descriptions of
it were partly wrong.** §11 says "01-08". `PLAN.md` said `login_screen.dart` plus four widgets.
Neither had been checked against the code, and the check is one command:
`grep -n "AppScaffold\|AppTextField\|AppButton" lib/tenancy/tenant_routing_shell.dart`. Screens 02
to 07 are phases of the routing shell and have been `AppScaffold` routes with `AppButton`s and
`AppTextField`s since steps 3 and 5a. Screen 08 is `_TenantBootstrapError`, one of the three
full-page `Center` states §5.1 names `LoadingState` / `ErrorState` / `EmptyState`, none of which
exists — giving one of them a bespoke treatment inside step 9 is how a fourth empty state gets
written. So the surface was **01**, and 01 was the last place in the app with a palette of its own.

**Every previous chunk this file mis-*counted*. This one it mis-*scoped*.** A session reading §11
would have opened seven already-migrated screens and concluded the step was mostly done; a session
reading `PLAN.md` would never have looked at them at all.

### What was decided

1. **It is a `Scaffold` carrying a `PageHeader`, not an `AppScaffold`.** `AppScaffold` is a toolbar,
   a header and a §4.2-capped body spanning the page. Sign-in has nothing for a toolbar — no way
   back from the app's front door and nothing to sign out of — so it would draw 56 logical pixels of
   empty chrome above the title. The decisive half is the wide layout: this screen is two panes and
   the title belongs to the **form**, not to a header spanning a form and a keypad. §7's page
   pattern is kept; the frame it usually arrives in is not. The raw-`Scaffold` count stays at 7 with
   this one's reason rewritten from "step 9" to a reason of its own.
2. **Whether the keypad appears is a measurement, and it replaces a breakpoint.** The screen asked
   §4.1 whether the window was 768 wide. §4.1's bands say how much room a *page* has; the question
   this screen needed answered is whether half the window can hold ten keys at §9's 48dp target. It
   could not, and the arithmetic is written out here because the first draft of this entry wrote
   "38 pixels" from an estimate and the estimate was too kind: the old layout gave the keypad four
   ninths of the window and then spent 48 on the card's margin and 48 on its padding, so at 768 that
   is `768 × 4/9 − 96 = 245` for ten keys — **24 pixels of slot each and 13 painted** — and at 1023,
   the top of the band, it is still only 36 and 24. It had been that way since the file was written,
   under a boundary that looked correct because it named a declared constant.
   `PosKeyboard.minimumWidth` answers it now: ten targets, nine `space.8` gaps, the card's inset and
   the pane's margin, which is **632**, so the keypad appears at **1264** and above.
   **A screen consulting one variable is not the same as a screen asking the right question**, and
   this is the only place in the app where the two came apart.
3. **A keypad key is not an `AppButton`, and §5.2's own arithmetic is the reason.** §5.2 gives
   `AppButton` a minimum horizontal padding of `space.20` — 40 pixels before a glyph — and
   `PressSurface` reserves 8 more for the ring gutter. At §9's 48-wide minimum that leaves nothing
   for the character. A component cannot be used at a size its own specification forbids, so the key
   draws itself from the same §2 rows `AppButton` reads: `action.secondary` for container, label and
   border, `radius.pill` because §2.3 restricts the pill to buttons and a key is one, `label.lg`,
   and `PressSurface` for press, hover, ring and target. Nothing invents a token.
4. **The refusal is an `AppNotice`, and this screen was the ninth notice surface rather than none of
   them.** It held a `String?` painted `Colors.red` — the exact half-model the seven back-office
   surfaces shed hours earlier. It was missed because the grep that found those is
   `grep -n "\-notice'" lib` and this screen's key was `login-error`. It is `login-notice` now, so
   the next run of that grep finds it.
5. **One of its branches was never a refusal.** `network-request-failed` — *"This device could not
   reach the server"* — is §2.1's `info`: nothing was refused, because nothing was answered. It had
   been drawn identically to a wrong password. `SignInFailureKind` carries the distinction, decided
   in the one `switch` that already owned the words so a second table cannot disagree with it. An
   unrecognised failure stays **refused** and not unknown: the *cause* is unknown, the *outcome* is
   not, and §2.1's `attention` means "awaiting".
6. **A defect this screen found itself sits on the field it is about; a provider answer sits in the
   page notice.** §5.2 gives a field an error line that replaces its helper, and §9 asks that a form
   error be associated with its input. "Enter the password for this account." is about one box;
   "That email address and password do not match an account." is about the credential, and a
   credential is not a box.
7. **The double border is closed, and the repair brought a test the diagnosis did not have.** Since
   commit `1b2b13b` on 2026-08-10 every login field painted two: `PillInput` set
   `border: InputBorder.none`, which was correct and stopped being sufficient the day `spiritTheme`
   gained `enabledBorder`, `focusedBorder` and `filled: true`, because `InputDecorator` prefers the
   specific slots over `border`. `AppFieldWell` strips all six and sets `filled: false`.
   `test/login_screen_test.dart` now pumps this screen **under `spiritTheme`** rather than a bare
   `MaterialApp` and asserts every slot — the whole mechanism of this defect is a theme reaching
   past a widget's own `border`, and a bare-theme test cannot see it.
8. **`Enter` is drawn disabled because it does nothing.** Its handler has been an empty branch with
   the comment `// Optional submit action` since the file was written. §2.1's disabled row is a
   rendering rather than a flag, so a control with no callback looks like one. Wiring it to submit
   is a behaviour change and `claude.md` hard rule 1 keeps that out of a visual step; dropping the
   key is a product decision. It is the same move §7's title chunk made when the staff directory
   stopped claiming to be read-only.
9. **The theme's checkbox went to §2.1, and what it cannot fix is recorded rather than hidden.**
   The tick was `Colors.green` at the call site over a theme painting `accentGreen` — two greens for
   one control — and the check mark was `bgDark`, the *page* colour, which is the divergence
   `onPrimary` carried until step 3. Both read `action.primary` now and the outline reads
   `action.secondary.border`. **What is still wrong is a new open decision**: an unticked checkbox's
   outline is the only thing saying the control exists, so it carries meaning under §9's own
   2026-08-12 reading and owes 3:1 — and `border.strong` is 1.97 on `surface.base` while
   `border.subtle` is 1.38. There is no third border role and `claude.md` forbids inventing one.
10. **Three copy changes, and only one of them is a copy decision.** `UNLOCK REGISTER →` became
    `Sign in`, which is §8 rule 3 naming *Unlock register* in its own list of what a control must
    never say. `EMAIL / USER ID` and `PASSWORD` became sentence case, which is §2.2 and §8 rule 7 —
    the *words* are unchanged, because what those fields should be called is step 11's. And the
    password placeholder `Enter Password` was deleted, because §5.2 says a placeholder is an example
    and never a restatement of the label.

### Two things a rendering found that no review would have

**The backspace key was a tofu box.** `⌫` is U+232B ERASE TO THE LEFT and Roboto does not carry it,
so the first picture of the new keypad showed an empty rectangle where the key's entire face should
be. It is the same defect `PLAN.md` already records against the bulk report's before/after arrow
(`bulk_catalog.dart:1590`), one step worse — a missing mark inside a sentence is a blemish, and a
control whose only face is a box cannot be named at all. It is `Icons.backspace_outlined` at
`AppButton.iconSize` with a semantic label, which is §9's icon-only row, and the Material icon font
*is* loaded beside Roboto in the harness.

**The general form is now a standing trap**: a glyph outside the Latin ranges is an asset rather
than a character, this repository's fonts have neither of the two it uses, and a string literal
outside ASCII needs a picture before it ships.
`grep -nP "[^\x00-\x7F]" lib --include=*.dart` finds the class; the harness finds the ones that fail.

**The second was a defect in this chunk's own first draft.** The pane padded 20 *and* the card
padded 20, so every key came out **44** wide against a component that had just promised 48 — and
what caught it is the test asserting `minimumWidth` against the rendered `PressSurface` rather than
against itself. The margin moved inside `PosKeyboard` so it is a term in the component's own sum,
and the pane now adds nothing. That is the "assert a published number against the rendering" lesson
the column-arithmetic chunk wrote, paying for itself the next day.

### Safety

No repository call, no state logic, no routing condition and no API shape changed. `_submit` sends
the same three arguments to the same boundary in the same order, refuses the same two input defects
before sending, and stays loading after a success for the same recorded reason. `git diff` and
`git status` over `functions/`, `firestore.rules` and `rules-tests/` print zero lines.

**Two behaviours did change and both are named rather than left to be noticed.**
`enableInteractiveSelection: false`, which `PillInput` set with the comment *"Prevent
selection/highlight"*, is gone: `AppTextField` offers no passthrough, and adding one to carry a
sign-in quirk into "one pattern, everywhere" is the wrong trade — so a person can now select the
text in these two fields as they can in every other field in the app. And **the keypad no longer
appears between 768 and 1263**, which is decision 2: at those widths it was drawing keys below §9's
floor.

## An input is a pill again, and a keypad learns lower case - 2026-08-15

### Why this chunk, and why it is not a step

**The product owner asked for it, having looked at what §11 step 9 landed an hour earlier.** In
their words: they do not like the black input fields, they prefer how the fields looked on the
original sign-in screen — with leading and, for the password, trailing icons, and that style — and
they want a caps button on the on-screen keyboard. "All the input fields", not sign-in's.

**Two of the three things they asked for contradicted `design.md` outright**, which is what made
this a chunk rather than a patch:

- §5.2 specified a **`surface.sunken`** well. That is the near-black they disliked.
- §2.3 restricted **`radius.pill`** to buttons, in as many words, with an argument attached: "when
  *everything* is a pill — buttons, chips, filters, cards, inputs — the shape stops signifying."

`design.md` is the product owner's specification and amending it is theirs to do; `design.md` §0's
own order of operations is *change this document, change the token file, change the widgets,
regenerate the screenshots*. **So the specification moved first and the code followed**, and the
version went to **v0.4** because four of the amendments are breaking.

**Four decisions were put to the product owner before any code was written**, because each changes
every field in the app and getting one wrong means redoing a 72-image diff. They took all four
recommendations: a new `surface.field` role at `#1E3A2B`; `radius.pill`; leading icons on the fields
where the glyph is unambiguous rather than on all 41; and §9's ring **plus** the original glow.

### What was decided

1. **§2.1 gains `surface.field` `#1E3A2B`, and `surface.sunken` loses the input well.** It keeps the
   table header and the code block, which are the two uses that genuinely are recessed. **No new
   hex**: `#1E3A2B` is `green.700`, already a primitive, so v0.4 added a *role* — which is precisely
   what §2.1 tells a widget to do when it needs a colour that has none. It collides with
   `border.subtle` by value, deliberately and named in §2.1: they never meet, because a field well
   is bounded by `border.strong`.
2. **A field is now the lightest surface in the set.** The ordering runs `sunken` → `base` →
   `raised` → `overlay` → `field`, so a well is not recessed; it sits *on* the page as a pill. That
   reads as backwards until you look at it, which is why `tokens_test.dart` walks the five in order
   rather than the document merely asserting it.
3. **§2.3's pill stops being buttons-only, and the argument is kept rather than deleted.** It now
   does its work on chips, filters, badges and cards. **What it costs is written into §2.3 rather
   than discovered**: a button and a field share an outline, and what keeps them apart is the action
   tier's fill, the field's persistent label, and the field's left-aligned content. If those stop
   being enough, the honest fix is to take the amendment back rather than add a fourth distinction.
4. **§5.2 gains an optional leading icon at 18 — `AppButton`'s size, one of the two §5.2 names — and
   it is optional in the strong sense.** **17 of 41 fields carry one and 24 decline it**: address,
   password, phone, money, code, quantity, receipt and filter get a glyph; "Reason for this
   adjustment", "Business name" and "Note" do not. The alternative was offered to the product owner
   and declined, and the reason is worth keeping: 24 of the glyphs would have been chosen to fill a
   slot rather than to say anything.
5. **The focus glow is back and §9's ring is still in front of it.** The original drew a glow
   *instead* of a ring, which is the §9 failure `DESIGN-AUDIT.md` §4.4 named. v0.4 draws both, and
   the test asserts the *pairing* rather than the glow: `accentGreen` at 30%, blurred 8, spread 1,
   behind the 2px ring at a 2px offset. §2.1 gains the one shadow it permits, on the grounds that a
   focus glow is an interaction state and not depth.
6. **The placeholder moved from `text.tertiary` to `text.secondary`, and that one is arithmetic
   rather than taste.** `text.tertiary` measures **4.29:1** on `surface.field` against §9's 4.5
   floor, where it measures 5.9 on the page. It was computed by hand before the change was proposed,
   flagged to the product owner as a risk in the same breath as the recommendation, and confirmed to
   the second decimal by `tokens_test.dart` afterwards. It is asserted **at the figure** rather than
   at a floor, so a later session that "restores" `text.tertiary` fails a test that explains itself.
   **Helper text is untouched** — it sits outside the well, on `surface.base`.
7. **The 1px `border.strong` stays, and the reason is functional.** §5.2 switches the border to
   `status.problem.border` on error. A well with no border has no error border — and the original
   `PillInput`, which drew none at rest, had no error state at all.
8. **`inputDecorationTheme` moved with it**, which is the half `AppFieldWell` cannot reach. Every
   field in the migrated tree strips that theme; what still reads it is the sale path's two
   unmigrated `TextField`s and the legacy island. Leaving it on `bgMid` at radius 14 would have left
   the one screen a cashier uses most with two dark rectangles while every other field in the app
   became a pill — and the request was *all* the input fields. **Its `hintStyle` had to move or it
   would have disappeared**: it was `mutedGreen`, which is `#1E3A2B`, which is now the fill.
9. **The keypad has a caps lock, and it fixes something as well as adding something.** Every letter
   key used to insert its upper-case identifier, so this keypad typed `OWNER@EXAMPLE.COM` and could
   **not type a lower-case password at all**. Off is now the default — an address is conventionally
   lower case and a password is case-sensitive — and `Caps` latches. **The key faces change with
   it**, so a person sees which case they will get rather than finding out by typing.
10. **`Caps` is one flex unit and an icon, and arithmetic forced both.** A labelled `Caps` needs two
    units, which would make the `Z` row 11 units and narrow every key in the keypad below §9's 48.
    So `PosKeyboard.columns` is now **measured over `rows`** rather than hardcoded to 10: the next
    key added widens the pane the keypad asks for instead of silently shrinking every key. That is
    the constant this repository has been burned by, caught one edit before it would have been
    wrong.
11. **A latched key is §2.1's `primary` tier**, the one tier that fills its container, so `Caps` is
    filled and mint among bordered ones. §9's "never hue alone" is satisfied by the fill, the glyph
    and the announcement together — a screen reader hears `Caps, on`.

### Safety

No repository call, no state logic, no routing condition and no API shape changed. `git diff` and
`git status` over `functions/`, `firestore.rules` and `rules-tests/` print zero lines.

**One behaviour changed and it is the one that was asked for**: the keypad types lower case by
default where it always typed upper case. Nothing else about what any field does moved — the same
controllers, formatters, validators, keyboard types and submit handlers, because the change is
entirely inside `AppFieldWell`'s chrome and `AppTextField` passes everything through as it did.

background runner was stopped: killing the npm wrapper does not kill the emulator it spawned.

## The home stops being eleven identical pills - 2026-08-16

`design.md` §11 step **5b, first half**: §4.4's navigation model, as a card grid below 1024 and a
side menu at or above it. The second half - lifting that menu into `AppScaffold` so it draws on
every route - is not in this chunk and is the next one.

### What the product owner decided first, and why it is not this chunk's

Three calls arrived before any code, and all three are recorded in `design.md` **v0.5** rather than
here.

**§4.4's four-destination bottom bar was drawn and then rejected.** Five mockups came back - a
device-queue panel, a compact page, the shift banner's three states, an expanded page with a rail.
Mapping the landing route's **eleven** controls onto *Sell / Stock / Money / More* put **five of
them in `More`**, which made the overflow bucket the largest destination in the app against one
control in *Sell*. The objection was the tap that bucket charges every control that did not make
the top three, and it is correct: a card home puts all eleven one tap from the front page.

**The till is pushed, never mounted.** Asked as "is the till a destination or a route", and the
evidence settled it rather than taste: the cart is a plain in-memory `Map<String, int>` at
`checkout_cart_panel.dart:168`; `checkout_draft.dart` builds a draft only at save time - *"refused
before anything durable is written"* - and `CheckoutRecoveryCoordinator` is confirmation-only for
sales already in the outbox. So a mounted till would make an unsaved cart's survival depend on
`IndexedStack` keep-alive, which is not a rule anyone would choose to write down. Pushing is also
what already ships, so this chunk never reached `checkout_draft`, `checkout_recovery` or
`checkout_outbox`.

**The home's title is `branding.companyName`, falling back to `membership.tenantName`.** This closes
the standing decision that left step 5a's last raw `Scaffold` alone. It turned out to be
ratification rather than a new rule: `tenant_branding.dart:53` already read
`branding?.companyName ?? fallbackName` and the call site already passed `membership.tenantName`.

### What was built

**`lib/ui/home_navigation.dart`** - `HomeDestination` and `HomeNavigation`, one component with two
renderings chosen by band, which is §4.3's own construction and `RecordList`'s. Two columns below
768, three to 1023, the side menu at 1024 and above. The primary spans its row at every band; the
rest are rows of `Expanded` under an `IntrinsicHeight`, because a `Wrap` sizes each child to its own
content and a row of cards with different label lengths is not a grid.

**A card carries its own condition**, which is the whole argument for this model over a tab bar -
`3 unresolved differences` and `shift open, 17 sales` are things a badge cannot say. It is optional
in the strong sense; a status that restates the label is noise.

**Every measurement is read from a §2 row written for something else** - `radius.md`,
`surface.raised`, `border.subtle`, `space.16`, `title.md`, `caption`/`text.tertiary`, and the glyph
at **18**, which is §5.2's leading-icon row. The same borrowing `AppSelect`, `Callout`, `Disclosure`
and `RecordActionSet` each made, and it is `PLAN.md`'s open question against §5.2 rather than this
file's. **The one figure with no row anywhere is the menu's width**, 256, which is a component
decision beside `AppScaffold.horizontalInset` and is now recorded next to it.

**The landing route** moved from a raw `Scaffold` to `AppScaffold`, which was the seventh of the
seven step 5a named and the last one that was ever going to be a step's rather than a component's.
Its eleven `AppButton`s in a `Wrap` became eleven `HomeDestination`s. **Every `onPressed` closure
and every visibility condition is unchanged** - the diff is the rendering and nothing else.

**`TenantBrandingPanel` stopped drawing the name and stopped loading it.** The route resolves the
document once, above its own header, and hands the result down; the panel keeps the slogan and the
session's standing. That removed a second read of a document the route had already fetched, so the
route makes fewer reads than before, not more. Its permanent notice also became a `Callout` - §5.1's
row for it, blocked until now only because the route was step 5b's and step 4's notice sweep could
not touch it.

### Two defects the screenshots caught and the tests did not

**Worth recording together, because they are the same mistake.**

**The primary card was drawn at 40% of its row, centred**, and the test that asserted it spans the
row passed. `PressSurface.fillWidth` fills the *hit area*; its `Align` then hands the child **loose**
constraints, so the painted `Container` shrink-wrapped its label and floated in a slot that was the
correct width. The test measured the slot - `find.byKey` reaches the `PressSurface`, not the card.
**The fix is `width: double.infinity` on the container**, and the test now measures the painted
`Container` rather than the key.

**The side menu came out 1156 wide against a declared 256.** A vertical scroll view hands its child
a *tight* width, and a `SizedBox` cannot shrink under a tight constraint. `Align` re-loosens it.

**Neither was visible in a passing suite and both were obvious in a picture**, which is the argument
`design.md` §10 makes for the screenshot diff being the review artefact. It is also the sharper half
of the same section's warning: a widget test proves the tree, and the tree was right.

**One shared component changed**: `PressSurface` gained `fillHeight`, `fillWidth`'s twin, defaulting
to false so nothing else moved. Cards beside each other need equal painted height, not merely equal
slots.

## The menu leaves the page and becomes the frame's - 2026-08-16

`design.md` §11 step **5b, second half**: §4.4's side menu lifted out of the home's body and into
`AppScaffold`, where the section says it belongs. With it, the two items the first half deferred -
the destinations ordered by frequency, and `HomeNavigation`'s §5.1 inventory row.

### What the section asked for, and the one part of it that is not built

§4.4: *"The side menu belongs to `AppScaffold`, not to a nested `Navigator`. `AppScaffold` is
already on every migrated route, so the menu renders on each one without routing moving and
`Navigator.pop` keeps meaning what it means."*

**The first sentence is built. The second is not, and the third is why.** The slot is in the frame;
25 of the 26 call sites leave it empty and the home fills it. **The menu draws on the home and on no
other route**, and that is a decision with reasons rather than an unfinished sweep. `PLAN.md`
carries it as an open decision for the product owner.

**A menu on a pushed route grows the stack, and that is the reason that decides it.** Every
destination on this route is a `Navigator.push`. Draw the menu on a pushed route and pressing three
destinations leaves the back arrow three routes deep, in a model where a person believes they are
switching sections; pressing the destination for the route they are standing on opens a second copy
of it. §4.4's own promise - `Navigator.pop` keeps meaning what it means - is what that breaks, so
the naive version of "every route" contradicts the sentence that authorises it. The two repairs are
a **nested `Navigator`**, which §4.4 forbids by name, and **popping to the home before pushing**,
which is a routing condition and is what `claude.md` hard rule 1 keeps out of a visual chunk.

**The destinations cannot reach a pushed route anyway, and this is the mechanical half.**
`MaterialApp(home: TenantRoutingShell(...))` puts the shell *below* the root navigator, so an
`InheritedWidget` installed in the shell is not visible to a route pushed onto that navigator. The
repository already proves it: `TenantSessionScope` is re-provided **27 times across 14 files**,
once at every push site, for exactly this reason. Carrying the destinations the same way is possible
and would be more call sites of the same kind - but it buys the stack-growth defect above rather
than avoiding it, so the reach problem is the cheaper argument and not the deciding one.

### What was built

**`lib/ui/scaffold.dart`** - `AppScaffold.navigation`, a `List<HomeDestination>` defaulting to
empty. At `expanded` with a non-empty list the body becomes a `Row`: the navigation column, then
`Expanded` holding the page. Below `expanded`, or with no destinations, the frame draws exactly what
it drew before and no call site's picture moves.

**A typed list rather than a `Widget` slot, which is the opposite of `primaryAction` on purpose.**
An action belongs to the page and the frame decides only where it sits; a navigation column belongs
to the *frame*, and §4.4 fixes its width, its band, and its relationship to the content maximum. A
`Widget` there would let any call site put anything in a 256-wide column beside every page and call
it navigation.

**The three questions `PLAN.md` queued inside this chunk, answered:**

- **The content maximum is measured against what is left, not against the window.** The menu costs
  `horizontalInset + menuWidth` = 276, so at 1440 a records page is **1164** and §4.2's 1200 does
  not fire; at 1600 it does, and the page is centred in the 1324 beside the menu rather than in the
  window. A maximum still measured against the window would ask for 1200 in a 1164 space.
- **The menu scrolls independently.** Eleven rows are about 600 tall and `expanded` puts no floor
  under the *height* - 1024 x 600 is a landscape tablet and a half-height desktop window - so a
  column that could not scroll would stripe the bottom of the navigation on the one band that has
  it. Its scrollable is its own, so scrolling a long table does not carry the destinations off the
  top, which is the whole point of a persistent menu.
- **A pushed route shows no menu.** Above.

**`lib/ui/home_navigation.dart`** - the single constructor became **two**: `HomeNavigation.cards`
and `HomeNavigation.menu`. The two renderings now have two *hosts* - the cards are content and sit
in the page below the shift panel, the menu is chrome and sits beside the page, outside the content
maximum and outside the page's scroll - and one constructor cannot say which host is asking.

**The band still owns the form and the host owns nothing but placement**, which is what keeps §4.3's
row true. `.cards` draws the grid below 1024 and nothing at or above it; `.menu` draws the menu at
1024 and above and nothing below it. The pair is **exhaustive and disjoint at every width**, which
is asserted directly: both hosts mounted in one tree at five widths draw eight destinations in
total, never sixteen and never none.

**The landing route** hands one list to both hosts. The destination list moved out of the body into
`_destinations(context)`, **reordered by frequency with the two account controls last** - New sale,
read-only catalog, manage catalog, daily summary, find a receipt, checkout settings, activity log,
staff directory, then *Change business* and *Make default*. That is the order
`tool/screenshots/home_navigation_test.dart` has been photographing since the first half, so the
pictures and the route now agree rather than a new order being invented here. **Every condition,
every role check and every closure is byte-for-byte what it was**; source order is what a grid
renders, which is why §4.4's ordering had to be applied to the list rather than to a layout.

**The gap above the cards goes with the cards.** §4.4 says the home "keeps its content and loses its
cards" at `expanded`, and a page whose last section is absent should not end on the space that used
to separate it.

**`design.md` §5.1** gained its `HomeNavigation` row - priority 1, replacing "a `Wrap` of eleven
identical pills", which is §4.4's own description. Recorded rather than invented: both values are
read off §4.4 and §11's step number.

### What the pictures showed

**Nine images changed, none added, none removed**, measured the way `PLAN.md` asks for rather than
reasoned about: the eight changed files were reverted to `HEAD` in place, the harness re-run to
produce a true baseline, the sources restored, and the two sets of 253 MD5s compared. Both runs are
the same side of midnight UTC, which is the other half of that trap.

          web / 95-home-navigation-owner, -cashier, -stateful

permissions. A run writes **253** and the directory now holds 253.

## Ten chunks in, the till has had none of it - 2026-08-16

Not a chunk. The product owner asked why the reskin feels like it delivers little visible UI per
session and why the app still looks half-baked, and the answer changed what is queued. Recorded here
because `PLAN.md` carries the queue and this file carries the reason.

### The arithmetic, which is the smaller half of the answer

Over the 27 commits of the design migration:

```text
docs (PLAN, HISTORY, design.md)   16,884   37.6%
lib/  (product code)              15,362   34.2%
test/                             10,155   22.6%
tool/ (screenshots)                2,479    5.5%
```

**Two-thirds of the churn is not product code, and the documentation alone outweighs it.** One
caveat in fairness to the figure: `numstat` counts additions *and* deletions, `PLAN.md` rewrites
large blocks each session, and `doc_index.dart` regenerates both indexes every time — so 37.6%
overstates the docs somewhat, though not by half. `PLAN.md` is 5,342 lines and `HISTORY.md` is
24,262.

**The screenshot share is not overhead of the same kind**, and this file should say so rather than
let one number condemn all four rows. Step 5b's first half shipped two defects — a primary card
painted at 40% of its row, a menu drawn 1156 wide against a declared 256 — that a fully passing suite
could not see and a picture caught immediately. **The test share is the more questionable one**: for
a migration whose first rule is that it never changes behaviour, a large part of those 10,155 lines
exists to assert that nothing moved.

### The structural half, which is the real answer

**The sale path has had none of the redesign, and it is the screen a cashier uses all day.**
`web/15-new-sale-with-a-cart` still shows a raw `Scaffold` with no `PageHeader`, Material fields, a
quantity control with a minus and a bin and no plus, Material chips for the tender row, a total in
inline body text, and permanent prose that should fold.

**The sharpest single piece of evidence is that §2.1's own worked example is still on screen.** That
section reads: *"The rule that fixes the sale screen: **Clear this sale** is `destructive`, **Save
sale** is `primary`. Today the destructive action is the more prominent of the two."* Ten chunks
later, "Clear this sale" is still the full-width prominent control and "Save sale" is still grey.
`AppButton` has had four tiers and six states since 2026-08-11.

**Thirteen of §5.1's twenty-five components do not exist**, checked rather than assumed — no class
matches `FilterChipBar`, `EmptyState`, `ErrorState`, `LoadingState`, `SyncIndicator`, `Pagination`,
`ConfirmDialog`, `AppSheet`, `AppTabs`, `LedgerEntry`, `QuantityStepper`, `RollingNumber` or
`MotionAsset` anywhere in `lib/`. Those are the rows that make a screen read as finished rather than
as consistent. The "Checkouts stored on this device / Saved offline: 2 / Submitting: 0" block on the
home is §5.1's own description of what `SyncIndicator` replaces: *"five-line offline queue list"*.

**§11 is breadth-first substrate, and that is the diagnosis.** Ten of its twelve numbers went to
things that apply everywhere and show nowhere in particular — tokens, buttons, fields, page frames,
record lists, figures, copy. The two numbers left are **7 (the till)** and **10 (motion)**, which are
exactly the two a person *feels*. Nothing in this app animates beyond the route transition. The
ordering is defensible — a screen with no tokens cannot be skinned — but its predictable consequence
is an app that reads as uniform rather than designed, with its highest-traffic screen untouched, and
**that consequence was never written down until now.**

### What it changed

The queue. The session that finished step 5b queued the end of step 4's sweep —
`receipt_lookup_panel.dart` and a tail of one- and two-`textTheme` files — **and queued it because it
was unblocked rather than because it was worth much.** That is the wrong selection rule and it is
what produced the complaint above.

**Step 7's unblocked half is queued instead.** The split is in `PLAN.md`: the tier inversion, the
page frame, the two fields, the twelve `textTheme` reads, the total and the prose all use components
that exist and are tested; `QuantityStepper`, `FilterChipBar`, `ConfirmDialog`, `AppSheet` and
`RollingNumber` are named as the remainder and **must not be guessed at**. `AppSheet` blocks the
responsive half specifically — §4.3 gives `Sale` "products + cart sheet" below `expanded` — so what
ships is the two-pane screen in real components, and the sheet comes back as a specification request
with a picture attached.

**The measurement, taken rather than carried.** `lib/checkout/checkout_cart_panel.dart`: 1 raw
`Scaffold`, 7 Material buttons (2 `OutlinedButton`, 2 `TextButton`, 3 `FilledButton`), 2 Material
`TextField`s, 12 `textTheme` reads. **This is the first inherited figure in six to survive
re-measurement.** Two that no previous count had reached: 2 `IconButton`s, which are
`QuantityStepper`'s, and 4 `ChoiceChip`s, which are `FilterChipBar`'s.

### The rule worth keeping out of all of this

**"Unblocked" is not a selection criterion.** Every queue entry since step 9 has been chosen by what
could be started without a decision, and the result is ten chunks of substrate with the most-used
screen in the product untouched. Ask what a person looks at, then ask what is blocked — in that
order.

## The till gets the redesign, and seventeen answers stop being a colour - 2026-08-16

Two chunks in one session, at the product owner's direction: *"take all the remaining reskin chunks
and do them as one, with commits in between and tests at the end."* `claude.md` hard rule 4 is one
§11 step per branch and `PLAN.md` recorded the batching exception as spent, so this is a **second
exception, granted verbally by the product owner** and recorded here rather than assumed. It covers
step 7's unblocked half and step 4's sweep tail. It does **not** cover steps 10 and 12, which are
blocked on decisions nobody has made, and the chunk did not touch them.

### What "all the remaining reskin chunks" turned out to be

Three things were queued and only two of them were real.

**Step 7's unblocked half was real and the carried measurement was right.** Confirmed by grep that
`checkout_cart_panel.dart` is the *only* file in the migrated tree with a Material button or a
Material field left, outside `lib/pos/**`, `lib/screens/**`, `login_screen.dart` and `config.dart`.

**Step 4's sweep tail was real and four times larger than the queue said.** It was written down as
"headed by `receipt_lookup_panel.dart`, three `textTheme` reads". It is **fifty reads across
twenty-four files**, and **seventeen of them are not cosmetic at all**: they are a write's outcome
painted as `colorScheme.error`, or on one card `colorScheme.primary`, with no container, no glyph
and no word. That is §9's status-by-hue row failing pass/fail on seventeen surfaces, and the queue
had it filed under "screens nobody looks at".

**Step 11's copy backlog was not real, and this is the retraction.** All seven items in `PLAN.md`'s
code block were checked against the code and **all seven are already closed** - step 11 closed them
on 2026-08-15 and the entry survived because that session could not say which of the seven it had
taken. The arrow at `bulk_catalog.dart:1590` reads `from X to Y`; `_summary` agrees its verbs and
says so in a comment; a previewed row says `Would be corrected`; the staff badges read
`tenant_membership_labels.dart`; the placeholder is `name@example.com` and the label is
`Email address`; screen 28's variances say *fewer* and *short of*. The block is struck in `PLAN.md`
rather than deleted, because "we could not tell" is the thing that kept it alive.

### The till

**§2.1's own worked example was still on screen and is closed.** That section reads *"**Clear this
sale** is `destructive`, **Save sale** is `primary`. Today the destructive action is the more
prominent of the two."* It was: an `OutlinedButton` wearing the theme's mint outline, sitting above
a `FilledButton`. They are `AppButtonTier.destructive` and `AppButtonTier.primary` now, and the
picture in `web/15-new-sale-with-a-cart` is the review artefact for it.

What else landed, all in components that already existed: the raw `Scaffold` became `AppScaffold` +
`PageHeader` at **`AppContentWidth.full`**, which had been declared since step 6a and read by
nothing; the two Material fields became `AppTextField`s, **which is the whole of what was left of
step 3's call-site sweep**; twelve `textTheme` reads became tokens; four notice surfaces became
`AppNotice` drawn as `Callout`s, the eighth surface that component had been waiting for; the total
became a `StatTile`; the submission policy became a `Disclosure`; the `InkWell` on the product tile
became a `PressSurface`, which is the most-pressed control in the app finally getting §2.4's press.

**The band boundary moved, and §4.3 is why.** The split was 768 - this app's own inherited figure,
predating §4.3 saying anything about a till. §4.3 gives `Sale` *"products + cart sheet"* at
`compact` **and** `medium`, and two panes only at `expanded`, so a 900-wide tablet gets the sheet
now. The cart pane is `AppLayout.salePane`, 420, **the last of §4.2's three widths with no reader**.

**Three things it found.**

1. **A `StatLine` on the compact cart bar overflowed at 411.** It is a label column and a
   right-aligned figure column, sized for a card where several stack; a strip with one figure has no
   column to line up with, so the two columns fought over about 200 pixels. The bar states its total
   as one `numeric.body` line instead. §2.2's complaint about figures inside sentences is about a
   *column* of them not lining up, and the role is what matters when there is no column.
2. **§7 and §2.1 disagree about a destructive confirm and neither can be followed without the
   other breaking.** §7 asks for *"`action.destructive`, **filled**"*; §2.1's destructive row is a
   transparent container with a red label and a red border, and there is no filled destructive
   container anywhere in the token layer. The confirm takes §2.1's tier and the disagreement is an
   open decision. Inventing the container is what `claude.md` forbids.
3. **The widget test's overflow was a font-metric artifact and the layout was sound.** "Open the
   cart" measured 195 logical pixels in a test face at one glyph per font size and about 95 in
   Roboto; the harness capture at 411 shows the bar comfortable. This is the standing "a widget test
   cannot measure text" trap arriving from the direction where it makes you *change* something that
   was fine - the fix was the `StatLine`, not the label.

**Still Material, each named rather than approximated**: `QuantityStepper` (§5.1 priority 1),
`FilterChipBar`, `ConfirmDialog`, `AppSheet`, `RollingNumber`. The `Quantity` field's persistent
label repeated down three cart lines is the clearest argument for the stepper existing; it is
correct per §5.2 and verbose, and it is the component's to fix.

### The sweep

Seventeen surfaces converted, every key preserved. **Four assertions in the whole suite needed
changing**, all four `Text.data` reads that became `Callout.message`, and they went through
`test/support/notices.dart`, which already existed for exactly this and says in its own doc comment
that it is a destination rather than a migration seam.

**The verification card is the sharpest case in the family.** Three answers - accepted,
undeliverable, refused - told apart by `colorScheme.primary` against `colorScheme.error` against
`colorScheme.error`. They are `ok`, `problem` and `problem` now, and the two that share a status
share it for a reason that is written down: an address the provider will not deliver to is
`problem` rather than `attention`, because `attention` means *awaiting* and nothing here is awaited.

**One judgement went against a fresh reading of `design.md`, deliberately.** §2.2 gives a section
head `title.lg`. Ten migrated screens shipped `title.md` for one - `Reconciliation runs`, `Paid by`
and eight more. The tree wins, and the reason holds up: at §4.1's `compact` band `PageHeader` gives
the **screen** title `title.lg`, so a section head at the same role puts two titles of equal weight
on a phone, which is what §7's "title appears once" is about. **The till's three section heads were
added at `title.lg` earlier the same session and are corrected to `title.md` in the sweep's own
commit** rather than left as a second convention - a design system with two answers to one question
is the failure §1 describes, arriving through consistency instead of through colour. The
contradiction is an open decision in `PLAN.md`; a sweep is not where it gets settled.

**Eleven expression-bodied `build`s became block bodies** to carry a `tokens` local, which is where
the line count is: **370 lines of real change under `git diff -w`, against 2,400 with the
reindentation counted.** `dart format` was deliberately not used - it reports 48 of 114 files in
these directories as unformatted, so running it would bury the change in an unrelated diff.

### Tests and pictures

| Suite | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Flutter | **2013 → 2022** (+9), then 2022 unchanged through the sweep |
| Functions | 409, ~32 s |
| Rules | 161 |
| Reconciliation integration | 10 |
| Invitation integration | 23 |

`git diff` over `functions/`, `firestore.rules` and `rules-tests/` printed **zero lines** across
both commits, and the four server-side suites were run over that to say so.

The nine new Flutter tests are the till's: the two tiers, the loading row replacing the label swap,
the four notice statuses, the `Disclosure` summary inside its budget, §4.3's `medium` band getting a
sheet, `showsTwoPanes` at 1023 and 1024, and the cart pane measuring 420. Three more are the
sweep's: `AppStatus.problem` on two refusals and `AppStatus.ok` on the verification card's
acceptance, which is the assertion the old red `Text` could not carry at all.

**Images: 7 moved for the till, 80 of 258 for the sweep, none stale and none removed.** Both
baselines were regenerated from `HEAD` immediately before comparison, per the standing trap - for
the till that meant stashing the two files, running the harness, popping, and running it again. The
sweep's 80 are mostly the heading role moving 16 to 18, which reflows every page that has one.

### What this chunk did not do, and why

**Step 10** needs three of §12's own open questions answered - is there a character, who builds the
Rive files, what is the floor device - and two §5.1 components that do not exist. **Step 12** is
blocked on six open decisions. Neither is startable without inventing something, and the product
owner's instruction was to do the remaining *reskin* chunks, not to guess at the specification.

### The rule worth keeping out of this one

**A sweep is where a convention gets applied, not where it gets chosen.** This chunk hit one place
where `design.md` and the migrated tree disagree, and the temptation was to "fix" twenty-four files
towards the document in the same pass that was touching them anyway. The cost of being wrong is
twenty-four files of churn plus an argument with whoever chose the other reading; the cost of
following the tree and raising it is one paragraph. Follow the tree, raise the contradiction, and
let the product owner spend the churn if they want it.
