## Two families the design named and the repository never had - 2026-08-22

`OPEN_QUESTIONS.md` decision 20 said bundle Hanken Grotesk and JetBrains Mono. Verifying it before
planning turned up the part the decision did not say: **neither font existed anywhere.** Not in
`fonts/`, not in `assets/`, not in the 18 MB export. The export links both from
`fonts.googleapis.com`, which is exactly the thing an offline-first till cannot do and precisely why
the decision says bundle rather than fetch. The chunk therefore began with acquiring binaries, which
was the product owner's call and was taken before any file changed.

`google/fonts` carries only variable masters for both families. A variable font in Flutter needs
`fontVariations` on every style, and `copyWith(fontWeight:)` then silently does nothing — a widget
asking for bold would get the default instance and no error. Static instances keep the ordinary
weight mechanism working, so the faces came from the upstream OFL repositories instead:
`marcologous/hanken-grotesk` at 400/500/600/700, `JetBrains/JetBrainsMono` at 400/500. Both licences
ship beside them. The first attempt, Google's `css2` endpoint under a legacy user agent, returned a
57 KB blob whose first four bytes are `88e0 0000` — not a TrueType, not a WOFF, a dynamically
subsetted thing. Checking the magic number is worth the one command it costs.

### The half of the change that mattered was not the fonts

`spiritTheme` had carried `fontFamily: 'Roboto'` since 2026-08-16, and **it was never reaching five
of the component themes.** A component theme's text style *replaces* the text theme's rather than
merging onto it: `ListTile` takes `listTileTheme.subtitleTextStyle` outright when it is set, so a
style built from an `AppTypeRoles` role that names no family arrives at the engine with none, however
`ThemeData` is configured. `ListTile`, `Chip`, `InputDecoration`, `SnackBar` and `Dialog` were all in
that position.

Nothing showed it, because `tool/screenshots/harness.dart` had been papering over it since the
harness was written — re-applying a family to nine component themes by hand, one `copyWith` each.
That is why every screenshot looked right while the app did not, and why the note in `theme.dart`
claiming the 2026-08-16 change "moves almost no image" was true for the wrong reason.

So all twelve roles now name a family rather than only `mono`. That fixed it at the source, and the
harness override is gone: `screenshotTheme()` returns `spiritTheme` unmodified, which is the property
that makes a capture evidence rather than a picture of a theme nothing ships.

### Families only, and the metrics are a question now

Every size, weight, line height and tracking value stayed exactly where it was. The scale is still
`design.md` §2.2. Profound Verdant's seven type roles disagree with it on almost every metric —
`section-title` is 600 where `titleLarge` is 500, `data-mono` is 14/500 where `mono` is 13/400,
tracking is stated in `em` throughout where `AppTypeRoles` stores logical pixels — and five app roles
have no design counterpart at all. Two of the reconciliation's own mappings are unsettled: it pairs
`headline-lg` with "`display` **or** `titleLarge`" without choosing, and pairs `section-title` with
`titleMedium` at `titleLarge`'s size.

That is `OPEN_QUESTIONS.md` question 22, raised rather than answered, and it is the only open item in
the file. Guessing it would have been the radius mistake again: decision 19 was taken from the
frontmatter, and the served artifact turned out to contradict both the frontmatter and the prose.

**JetBrains Mono is declared at 400 and 500 where the decision says 500.** `AppTypeRoles.mono` reads
400 and this change moved no metric. Declaring 500 alone would not have failed — the engine picks the
nearest declared face — so the token would have claimed 400 and rendered 500 with nothing anywhere
saying so. One extra file buys an honest token and costs the `data-mono` repoint no download.

### A stale instruction, found by verifying rather than by reading

`OPEN_QUESTIONS.md`'s "coupled consequence of decision 21" still told the reader that moving
`AppLayout.expandedFloor` from 1024 to 1280 was a mandatory second step that had to land with the
first or the sale path regresses. Step one landed; **step two never did and will not.**
`TOKEN_RECONCILIATION.md` item 6 had already recorded 1024 as the deliberate deviation, and the code
agrees with it, so the section now carries a dated correction pointing at the newer decision. Its
other half survives: no harness viewport covers 1024 to 1279, and the four behaviours that flip there
are rendered by nothing. That viewport is the next chunk.

### Tests and evidence

A repointed assertion and a new one. The repointed one is the family test, on its third value now —
"no role names a family", then "only mono, and it names Roboto Mono", now every role with `mono`
named separately. The new one is a source scan of `pubspec.yaml`: it fails if any role names a family
or a weight the pubspec does not declare. That failure is otherwise invisible, because a missing
weight does not throw — the engine substitutes the nearest declared face, so a 600 renders as a 500
and only a person holding both files finds out. The harness carries the same list a third time and
cannot read it from a test binary, which has no asset bundle; its doc comment says the lists move
together.

2,249 tests pass. The shipped `FontManifest.json` was read out of the built APK rather than out of
`build/flutter_assets/`, which was stale and still listed Roboto — the APK's own manifest declares
the two families at the six weights and no Roboto at all. Worth knowing: the incremental asset
directory keeps undeclared leftovers, so the APK still *contains* the Roboto files it no longer
declares. Undeclared is not bundled behaviour, but a clean build is what actually removes them.

**Not verified on a device.** The connected phone dropped to `adb offline` and stayed there through a
full server restart, so the debug APK was built and never launched. Screenshots prove the raster and
the manifest proves what shipped; neither proves the app runs.

## The type scale moves, and the frontmatter is right this time - 2026-08-22

Question 22 was raised and answered the same day, which is unusual enough to say why. The radius
repoint had been taken from `DESIGN.md`'s frontmatter and the served artifact turned out to
contradict it, so the standing instruction became check the artifact. Doing that here produced the
opposite result: normalising the served Tailwind `fontSize` config across all 76 exported screens
collapses **31 apparent variants to whitespace and quoting**, and 75 of the 76 are value-identical
and agree with the frontmatter. One outlier states `data-mono` 13 / 1.2 and `section-title` 20, and
is outvoted 75 to 1.

**The lesson is not "never trust the frontmatter".** It is that the check is cheap and the answer
differs per token family. Colour agreed, radii did not, typography does. Skipping the check is what
cost the radius decision, not the source it read.

### Three decisions, and one the evidence overturned

The product owner took all three: adopt the seven named roles and derive the other five; map by size;
add a sibling compact role rather than a resolver. So `headline-lg` 32 goes to `display` 32 and
`section-title` 22 to `titleLarge` 22 — this file had hedged the first and paired the second with
`titleMedium` at 18, which the size contradicts. `displayCompact` at 28 is new, and it is the first
breakpoint-aware type value any source this app has had actually states; the call site picks by band,
because a token that silently means two things is the thing `AppSpacing`'s note argues against.

**The preview those decisions were taken against was wrong in one row, and the design says so
directly.** It proposed `labelLarge` at 16 / 600, inferred from the stock `text-base`. But
`.btn-primary` is *measured*: `font-size: 14px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.05em`, at
`height: 48px`. Measured beats inferred, so the button label is 14 / 700 / +0.7. Worth noting where
that 48px sits — §9's touch target turns up in the *design's* own CSS, not only in this app's rules.

The five roles with no named counterpart are not stranded on §2.2 either. The design uses stock
Tailwind sizes **1,028 times** alongside its seven (`text-sm` 475, `text-xs` 316, `text-lg` 78), so
they derive from what the screens actually use: `titleMedium` ← `text-lg`, `labelMedium` ← `text-sm`,
`caption` ← `text-xs`, `numericHero` ← `text-3xl`.

**One fragment of question 22 is deliberately still open.** The design sets money in `data-mono` —
65 of the places a `currency-kes` colour appears also carry `text-data-mono`. `numericBody` stayed in
the interface face with tabular figures anyway, because moving every price in the app into the mono
face is a composition judgement per surface, like the `mono` reader sweep, and not a metric.

**Correction to the entry above this one**, written earlier the same day: it says JetBrains Mono is
declared at 400 and 500 because "`AppTypeRoles.mono` reads 400 and this change moved no metric".
True when written and superseded within hours — `mono` is now `data-mono` exactly, 14 / 1.0 / 500
with -0.14 tracking. Bundling the 500 face turned out to be the right call for a reason other than
the one given: not honesty about a token that would have rendered 500 while claiming 400, but that
the repoint needed the face and it was already there.

### What moved, measured rather than estimated

**346 of 361 screenshots changed; 15 did not.** Three assertions outside the type tests moved, and
each is annotated where it sits rather than in a changelog:

- `AppButton`'s label 15 → 14, plus the weight, from the `.btn-primary` measurement.
- The safe-landing scrollable 551 → 548. Nothing in the frame's arithmetic changed; one of its inputs
  did — `section-title`'s 1.4 line height grows the page header's title from 28 to 30.8 and the body
  loses the difference. That test is written as a measurement precisely so this is legible.
- A compact row's content is **37** of its 40 minimum rather than 36, because `body-sm` states 1.5
  where §2.2 gave 20/14. It still fits, and it is now the tighter of the two measurements holding
  §3's "12 / 8" reading. Three pixels of headroom left.

Tracking needed a conversion: the design states `em` and `TextStyle` has only logical pixels. Every
figure is the design's `em` times that role's own size, and the test asserts the arithmetic rather
than the result, so the source stays checkable. **Four roles are tracked, not the three the
frontmatter names** — the fourth is the button, and only the CSS says so.

2,249 tests pass. `height: 1.0` on `label-caps` and `data-mono` was the one thing worth eyeballing
rather than asserting, because a line box tighter than the glyphs can clip descenders; the
regenerated component matrices show it does not.

**Verified on hardware, not only in the harness.** The debug APK was rebuilt on the repointed scale
and installed on the connected phone, and the sign-in route renders it: the button label visibly
bolder and tracked at 14 / 700 / +0.7, the field labels a size up, the headline tighter on both
tracking and leading. That path matters because it is not the harness's `FontLoader` — the faces
resolve from the APK's asset bundle, through the `InputDecoration` component theme that had never
had a family reach it at all. What a screenshot still cannot show is motion, and nothing here
touches any.

## Five regions on one axis, and the harness had three of them — 2026-08-22

First slice of the unsupervised run, and the cheapest one in the order of work: additive, no existing
pixel moved, and later phases inherit the coverage. Commit `7509dcc`.

**The gap was named as one region and is two.** `prompt.md` and `AUTONOMOUS_HANDOVER.md` both say the
same thing — no harness viewport covers 1024 to 1279, and the four behaviours that flip there
(`record_list.formFor`, `home_navigation.showsMenu`, `PageHeader.showsDisplayTitle`,
`routes._isExpanded`) are rendered by nothing. That is true. It is also not the whole shape of the
problem, and deriving the boundaries instead of taking the number is what showed why.

§4.1 declares two band floors, 768 and 1024. §4.2 declares two *page* maxima, 720 for reading and
1200 for records. Those are four boundaries on **one** axis and they **interleave**: 720, 768, 1024,
1200. So the axis is cut into five regions, not three, and a width can cross a maximum without
changing band or change band without crossing a maximum. The harness's own header said 1440 and 411
"straddle" both breakpoints and both content maxima, which is exactly true and has been read as
coverage ever since. Straddling four boundaries puts you in the outermost two of five regions.

The two dark ones:

- **1024 to 1199.** `expanded`, so §4.3's table; and under the 1200 records maximum, so the table
  fills the window rather than being capped. The narrowest a table in this app is ever laid out, and
  with `HomeNavigation.menuWidth` beside it the content column is 768. It is also precisely the region
  the **deliberate 768/1024 deviation created** — Profound Verdant puts its desktop floor at 1280,
  and `OPEN_QUESTIONS.md` item 21 moved this app's to 1024 on the grounds that a table at 1194 beats
  stacked cards. Those 176 logical pixels are where that claim lives, and nothing showed it.
- **720 to 767.** Still `compact`, so stacked cards, no menu, and `title.lg` rather than `display`; but
  over the 720 reading maximum, so the column is capped and centred. Band and maximum look like one
  axis until a picture shows one firing without the other, and no picture did: 411 is compact and
  uncapped, 834 is capped in the middle band.

**Both new widths are boundaries rather than midpoints, and that was the one real choice here.**
`AppLayout.isAtLeast` is inclusive, so 1024 is the *first* width at which all four behaviours flip and
767 is the *last* width that is still compact. `test/ui/routes_test.dart` has asserted "exactly 1024 is
expanded" for a while, so the arithmetic was already pinned and only the rendering was not — a picture
of the boundary is worth more than a picture near one. Heights are 768 and 1000: the first is the
window 1024 belongs to, the second matches the tablet already in the file.

**`AppLayout.salePane` is not a boundary**, and excluding it is what keeps the count at five. It is the
fixed width of a pane inside a page, set as a `SizedBox` at `checkout_cart_panel.dart:720`, not a
maximum applied to a page — so nothing about a screen changes when a window crosses 420.

### The rename, and what is deliberately not in the new list

`everyBandViewports` becomes `responsiveViewports`. With a fourth entry the old name states something
false, and 20 call sites is a mechanical rename that moves no pixel. `compactWideViewport` is
**deliberately absent from it**: for a component that varies by band and not by maximum, 767 is 411's
rendering stretched, and 20 more images of that is the diff nobody reads. That is not a new judgement
— `tabletViewport`'s own note has recorded it since step 6, which is why `tablet` was never in the
default pair either.

The content-width matrix is the one file whose subject is width itself, so it takes all five as
`everyRegionViewports` and goes from 6 pictures to 15. Its header had claimed six was "that matrix in
full", which was the matrix of a two-value width axis that does not exist.

**What the fifteen show that six could not:** `records` buys nothing until 1200. Its image is
byte-identical to `full`'s at 1024, 834, 767 and 411, and differs only at 1440. That is the arithmetic
— a `ConstrainedBox` at 1200 constrains nothing narrower than itself — but it is the fact a reader
gets wrong, because the row shape changes at 1024 and the cap fires at 1200 and this app's expanded
band starts in between.

### The tripwire, and why it is what found the second region

`test/ui/tokens_test.dart` now source-scans `tool/screenshots/harness.dart`, derives the four
boundaries from `AppLayout`, and fails if any of the five regions is left with no viewport — naming
the interval in the message. A scan rather than an import, for the reason the pubspec font scan beside
it is one: `tool/` is outside `lib/` and a test binary has no asset bundle, so the harness can only be
read. Verified by deleting `desktopNarrowViewport` from the list, which fails with *No screenshot
viewport falls in [1024.0, 1200.0)*.

Writing the tripwire is what made 720-767 visible, and that is the order worth recording: the handover
asked for one viewport, and a tripwire that checked only the region it named would have been the
weaker artifact. So this slice went slightly beyond its brief, upward, and the run log says so.

### What moved, measured rather than estimated

**34 new images. None of the existing 361 moved, and none disappeared** — hashed before and after with
`sha256sum`, because `screenshots/` is gitignored and `git status` reports nothing whatever it holds.
23 in `desktop-narrow/`, 5 in `desktop-narrow-full/`, 3 in `compact-wide/`, and 3 in `tablet/`, which
the content-width matrix had not been capturing. The index is 149 screens.

The screenshot suite is 325 tests, up from 296; the client suite is 2,250, up from 2,249. Everything
passes, and `flutter analyze` on the four edited files is clean.

**One finding, and it is a Phase 04 question rather than a defect.** At 1024 a `RecordList` table's
action cell **stacks** its two buttons where 1440 lays them side by side, which makes a row about 145px
tall and fits four rows in the window instead of five. That is correct behaviour under the existing
widget and no logic was touched to produce it. It is now at
`screenshots/desktop-narrow/96-record-list.png`, which is the point of having the viewport.

**What this proves is the raster.** No screen overflows or truncates at either new width, which a
widget test does detect. It does not prove the app runs, and it cannot show motion; nothing in this
slice touches either.

Also observed and left alone: `build_index.dart`'s generated README still says the only faces loaded
are Roboto and the Material icon font, and that two glyphs render as tofu for that reason. Both
statements predate the typography repoint at `71f26c2` and are now wrong. Correcting generated prose is
a different reason to move text and belongs in its own commit.

## Wave 0's remainder, and the token layer that was not finished — 2026-08-22

Second and third slices of the unsupervised run, taken together because the second one found the
third. Commits `a77e95c` through `246fdfd`.

### The audit came first, and it said not to build four of the six

`prompt.md`'s Wave 0 list names six components — disabled, read-only, offline, busy, confirmation,
provenance — and the foundations audit had left all six unexamined. Read as a work list it is six
things to build. **Five of the six were already implemented**, and `audits/2026-08-22-wave-0-components.md`
records where each lives and which screenshot proves it:

- **disabled** is a state on six controls and every one is photographed. It is not a component, and
  `DESIGN_RULES.md`'s accessibility line agrees — it calls read-only and disabled *states*.
- **busy** is two facts with two treatments. `AppButton.loading` holds the container and is explicitly
  *not* disabled; `LoadingState` covers a read that has not answered, with a required message because
  the four things it covers on the routing shell alone are checking a sign-in, opening an account,
  opening a business and signing out.
- **confirmation** is `ConfirmDialog`, which has the widest matrix of the six already.
- **offline** is three treatments because it is three different facts, which is what `DESIGN_RULES.md`
  asks for by name.
- A page-level *everything is disabled* wrapper is ruled out by `RBAC_MATRIX.md` directly — *"A
  cashier home should remain intentionally narrow, not appear as a disabled manager dashboard"* — and
  the app already obeys it: `11-business-home-cashier`'s caption reads *"Four of the owner's buttons
  are absent rather than disabled."*

Building all six would have stood four competing systems next to working ones, which is the failure the
prompt's own working discipline names. **The audit was the deliverable, and its most useful sentence is
a negative one.**

### read-only was two facts wearing one word, and one site rendered it wrong

Six surfaces tell a person something cannot be changed. Five render an `info` `Callout` and they had
independently settled a two-tier pattern nobody had written down: **titled** for the standing of a
whole page, **untitled** for one control unavailable in this build. The sixth,
`checkout-configuration-read-only`, was a bare `Text` — no container, no glyph, no status role —
under the same `!canPublish` condition as `printer-configuration-read-only`, which is a `Callout`, in
the same feature folder.

**How it survived is the more useful half.** Three of the six notices appeared in **no capture at all**,
because every screenshot that reaches a build-gated branch injects the writer. The three that were
photographed are the three that stayed right. So the repair is three things:
`16b-checkout-settings-read-only` and `18c-manage-catalog-read-only` render those surfaces with no
writer, the rendering matches its siblings, and a source scan in `test/ui/status_test.dart` fails if a
`-read-only` key ever sits on anything but an `info` `Callout`. Nothing typed could catch it: a
`String` in a `Text` and a `String` in a `Callout.message` are the same `String`.

The print queue stays silent and stays outside the scan. It draws nothing when no retry is injected,
which `37c-receipts-waiting-read-only`'s caption records as the decision. And the role/build
distinction must not be merged: `staff-directory-read-only` fires on `session.canAccess` and names the
roles that can act, and `RBAC_MATRIX.md` has exactly one role-based read-only row.

### And then the picture of that fix showed a defect nine days old

`18c-manage-catalog-read-only` was a new capture of `Manage catalog`. Its **Categories** row rendered as
filled bars where the category picker four inches below it rendered words. Both are chips. The first is
a raw Material `Chip`; the second is a `FilterChipBar`.

`spiritTheme`'s own note said that naming a family on every `AppTypeRoles` role *"is what reaches the
component themes below"*. It reaches the ones that **read a role**. Four did not:
`chipTheme.labelStyle`, `chipTheme.secondaryLabelStyle`, `listTileTheme.subtitleTextStyle` and
`snackBarTheme.contentTextStyle` were written as `TextStyle(color: ...)` inline, and a component theme's
text style **replaces** the text theme's rather than merging onto it — so all four reached the engine
with a null family, a null size and a null weight, whatever `ThemeData.fontFamily` said.

**This is exactly the trap `AUTONOMOUS_HANDOVER.md` §8 predicted, still live, in three of the five
components it names.** And nothing in the repository said so: the colour tests enumerate all fifteen
`TextTheme` slots and find fifteen correct colours, because a colour is right or wrong independently of
a size; the type tests measure `AppTypeRoles` and never ask whether the theme reads it. A picture said
so, and had been saying so since the type repoint landed.

**The worse one was `02-choose-business`**, the second screen in the app: every membership's
*Owner — Accessible* line was an unreadable bar. It is a `ListTile` **subtitle**, and `ListTile.title`
was always fine — title merges onto the text theme, subtitle is taken as given. One half of one
component, which is why nobody looking at the screen noticed.

`chipTheme` now takes `label.md`, because that is what `FilterChipBar` already uses, so the app's chip
and Material's chip cannot disagree. `listTile`'s subtitle takes `body.md`: its old 13 was on no scale
at all, §2.2 has 12 and 14 and nothing between, and 14 is Material's own default role for a subtitle.
`snackBar` takes `body.md`. 46 of 401 images moved and every one is a screen with a raw `Chip` or a
`ListTile` subtitle.

The second half was three `TextTheme` slots this theme sets by hand, all three carrying a size §2.2
does not have. `headlineLarge` 40 against a 32 ceiling — zero readers, so zero pixels, repointed
anyway because a slot that says 40 is a figure somebody will eventually believe. `bodyMedium` a bare
`fontSize: 16`, inheriting Material's 20/14 leading where §2.2 states 16 / 24, which is every bare
`Text` in the app set on a 22.9 line box. `labelLarge` 15 / 600 against the design's **measured**
`.btn-primary` at 14 / 700, which `AppButton` already renders — so a `SegmentedButton` and a button
beside it disagreed on both a size and a weight. **122 of 401 images moved**, all of them surfaces with
bare `Text`.

`lib/theme.dart` now names **no type metric of its own at all**, and a source scan in
`test/theme_test.dart` fails on any `fontSize`, `fontWeight`, `letterSpacing`, `height` or
`wordSpacing` written as a number there, comments excluded so the file can still explain the figures it
removed. A second group resolves each affected Material component under the real theme and fails if the
family the engine is handed is not one of the app's two — `SnackBar` included, because no capture
drives one, so no picture will ever cover it.

**One assertion was wrong on the first pass and is corrected rather than deleted.** "Left without a
colour" cannot be tested as `color == null`: `ThemeData` applies its body and display colours to every
slot, so a style authored colourless still arrives carrying one. What the original note meant, and what
is asserted now, is that it arrives carrying the same ink as the text beside it.

### provenance was the one component genuinely missing

§5.2 specifies it in one line — `caption`, `text.tertiary`, the instant first and then the actor —
and nothing implemented it. The same `Text`-plus-style expression appeared **seven times across five
files**, four of them under a comment naming the section they were implementing by hand.

**It could not be fixed the way read-only was**, and the contrast is the useful part. Read-only was
pinned by a scan because there the rendering *is* the identifying feature. Here it is not: `caption`
with `text.tertiary` appears **29 times** in `lib/` and only seven are provenance — the other 22 are
stat details, cart notes, helper lines and figure captions, all correctly that pair and none of them
this. A scan would have flagged all 29. The concept needed a name.

The drift it prevents had already happened once and is left alone deliberately:
`stock_adjustment_panel.dart` folds a provenance string into a `Callout.message` after a newline, two
type roles from where §5.2 puts it. That one is genuinely part of a message rather than a row under
it.

`ProvenanceLine.styleOf` is public for one real caller and it is not a test. `RecordList`'s narrow-loss
allocator **measures** provenance to size the identity column, so before this the allocator named
`typography.caption` and the renderer named `typography.caption` and nothing tied them — a repoint of
one would have allocated the table's columns against a style nothing paints.

**0 of 401 existing images moved.** That is the proof the migration is faithful rather than
approximately faithful: the component draws what the seven sites drew, byte for byte. What did change
is what a test finds: `RecordItem.provenanceKey` now names the component, so 28 assertions across
eleven files ask `test/support/text.dart`'s `textAt` instead of casting to `Text`.

**A formatter-only commit sits in front of it**, and the reason is worth recording as a working rule.
Most of `test/` has drifted from the current `dart format` — a whole-tree run rewrites about ninety
files — so `dart format test/` was run once, produced 90 files of churn, and was reverted. §4's
"format the changed files only" means *do not leave your own new code unformatted*, not *reflow
everything the formatter now disagrees with*. Fifteen files were formatted as their own commit so the
provenance diff reads as 28 assertions rather than six hundred lines.

### the RBAC guards, and every row agreed

`RBAC_MATRIX.md`'s first line says it is derived from the active Dart authorization lists, which makes
it a snapshot — and a snapshot of authorization is the kind of document that is quietly wrong for
months. `test/tenancy/rbac_matrix_test.dart` holds one entry per row and asserts the guard behind it.
**All 31 named role lists hold exactly what the table gives them**, across 36 assertions, and nothing
in `lib/` needed changing.

Two maps rather than one, deliberately: one reads the app's constants so a failure names the symbol,
the other is authored from the matrix so the comparison means something. A single map would assert that
a list equals itself.

The assertion worth having is the completeness scan, and it is the only one here a reader would not
think to write: the set of role lists in `lib/` must be exactly the set the file knows about. Everything
else checks guards that exist, and a capability added next month with a list of its own would pass all
of them by not appearing.

**Route offering is deliberately not asserted, and the reason is a finding.** `lib/main.dart` feeds each
role-gated navigation slot the repository's own constant — `dailySummaryRoles:
TenantDailyMetricsRepository.allowedRoles` and eleven more of that shape — so the list the landing
route hides by and the list the repository refuses by are the **same object**. The matrix's *"Hidden
actions must also be guarded in product code"* holds by construction rather than by review. A test
would pass for the wrong reason.

Two rows gate a **scope** rather than a route, and the matrix now says so. A cashier opens shift history
and reads their own closed shifts; reading another cashier's is the management scope, and
`shift_history_panel.dart` hides the scope control behind the same predicate the repository enforces. A
manager reaches the staff directory and the screen's `_readOnly` is true exactly when the session holds
neither write gateway. The platform separation is structural too: the `superAdmin` claim is read in one
place, reaches the shell as one callback, and is consumed only by a routing phase carrying a
`PlatformReviewIdentity` rather than a `TenantMembership`.

**Not proven, and the test's own header says so:** the server. `firestore.rules` and the callables are
the real boundary and `rules-tests/` is where that is shown.

### the fixtures were clean, and checking them found 27 files nothing runs

The sweep found nothing: no forbidden branding, no invented roles, no tax, no refunds, no reorder
thresholds anywhere in `test/` or `tool/`. The screen captures use the seed script's own catalog and
categories exactly. `supplier` appears in the bulk-import tests only as a column the app **refuses**.

So the deliverable became keeping them correct rather than correcting them, because Wave 1 and Wave 2
compose the exact screens whose designs carry the invented facts — ST-048's `Ceramic Mug`, its
`Tax (16%)` line and its refund figures, ST-039's `Before/After` column. Eight tokens, each traced to
the document that forbids it. **The list is short because half the candidates are unscannable**: the app
already says *"the payment itself is not verified"* and *"the payment is unverified"*, and calls
*Cancel cash count* a reversal. A scan for `verified payment` or `reversal` would flag four sentences
that are right, and a tripwire that cries wolf teaches the next person to route around it.

**What the sweep turned up instead:** `CLAUDE.md` hard rule 3 names two dead directories and there are
ten. `lib/pos/**` and `lib/screens/**` are 52 unreachable files and are called out; **27 more, 4,627
lines across eight more locations, are equally unreachable from `lib/main.dart` and named by nothing.**
Several are actively misleading for this work. `lib/widgets/` is a **pill** component set and decision
19 is that the design has no pills at all. `lib/constants/colors.dart` and `lib/component/colors.dart`
are two more colour systems and `constants/sizes.dart` a rival size scale — the "competing local
design system" the prompt forbids **creating** is already there, three times over. `lib/model/` holds
supplier, customer and invoice models for capabilities the product does not have.
`fraud_detection_service.dart` is 556 lines of return-fraud analysis that `screenshots/README.md`
correctly lists under *Not pictured — scoped, not started*. `lib/config.dart` is 1,178 lines of which
**zero** are live code.

Recorded and pinned, **not deleted**: `lib/pos/**` is explicitly kept for its flow, and deleting 27
files is a substantial unrequested change. `test/dev/reachable_lib_test.dart` makes the set stable so a
file joining or leaving it is a decision. It also asserts the reachable set is closed, which is the
property that would break first if a live file started reading `lib/constants/colors.dart` for a hex.
`CLAUDE.md` gains three lines rather than a list, because that file loads on every turn and its own
first instruction is to stay short.

One cost paid: the first version of the closure read only the first URI of each directive and called
`checkout_print_transport_io.dart` dead. It is reached through `if (dart.library.io)` on a continuation
line. There is a test for that specific mistake now.

### What moved, measured rather than estimated

**2,314 tests pass, from 2,249** at the start of the run. The screenshot harness is 333 captures writing
**405 images, from 361**. Every figure below is a before-and-after `sha256sum` over `screenshots/`,
because that directory is gitignored and `git status` reports nothing whatever it holds.

| Commit | moved | new | gone |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `7509dcc` the two width regions | 0 | 34 | 0 |
| `19317d7` read-only | 0 | 6 | 0 |
| `ab04fff` four familyless component styles | 46 | 0 | 0 |
| `af81a2d` three type literals in the theme | 122 | 0 | 0 |
| `9df70c5` `ProvenanceLine` | **0** | 4 | 0 |

**What this proves is the raster.** No screen overflows or truncates, which a widget test does detect,
and the two font fixes are visible in pictures that were previously bars. It does not prove the app
runs, and it cannot show motion; nothing in any of these seven commits touches motion, and none of them
changes behaviour — no repository call, no state, no routing condition, no API shape.

## The sale path is composed, and both defects it was sent to fix were already fixed — 2026-08-22

Phase 03 is the first chunk of the unsupervised Stitch run that changes what a screen looks like.
Everything before it was tokens, components and contracts; what shipped until today was the app's
existing layout wearing Profound Verdant. Seven commits, `107cdea` to `82f2f50`, on
`stitch-wave-0-tokens`. Nothing pushed.

The brief pointed at three designs: ST-035, the reviewed desktop/tablet candidate; the recovered
mobile browse render; and ST-036, the mobile cart, carrying **two named defects to correct**.

### Both ST-036 corrections turned out to be nothing to do

`LIVE_PHASE_HANDOFF.md` says ST-036's save refusal invents a cause — *"Could not save sale. Storage
full or write error."* — and prescribes the app's established generic sentence instead. That sentence
is verbatim what `checkout_refusal.dart:202` has returned all along, for any code this build does not
model. And ST-036 renders a `Sale / Orders / History / Sync` bottom bar to be deleted; the reachable
app contains no bottom navigation of any kind, in any file. `grep` finds two hits and both are
commented out inside `lib/pos/`, which hard rule 3 makes read-only anyway.

So the phase's two named corrections are a third and fourth instance of the pattern the Phase 02 audit
found twice: **the app is right where the design is wrong.** Neither cost a line of code. What they
cost is worth recording anyway — checking them is what a handover's defect list is for, and the answer
being *no change* is a result rather than a non-result. `15c-sale-refused` now photographs the refusal
that was previously reachable only from a widget test.

### What actually changed

The till was three surfaces in one file and each was one long scroll.

**The browse pane** is a fixed head over a scrolling grid now, which is what both designs draw. The
reason is not tidiness: a cashier who scrolled to the twentieth product lost the search field off the
top of the screen, and typing a name is the fastest way to reach a product. The tile became two tiles
chosen by band, because the two designs *are* two tiles — a dense text card with the scanner's code on
it where the cart is already on screen, and a picture-led card carrying a count of what is rung up
where the cart is behind a tap. The grid extent moved 230 → 260, which is the single number that gives
this app the column counts both designs ask for at every band: two on a phone and a tablet, three at
1024, four at a till.

**The cart pane** became a head, a scrolling middle and a foot. On a phone it had been one `ListView`,
so a cashier with six items scrolled past all six to reach the save and the total went off the top
while they did. The clear moved into the head — ST-035's arrangement, and it finishes §2.1's own
worked example, because the destructive action and the primary one are now at opposite ends of the
pane rather than adjacent.

**The two-region till** separates its panes with depth rather than with a hairline the same weight
this app uses between two rows of one list.

### Money got a colour, for one surface

`currency-kes` `#45F28D` had sat in the palette wired to nothing since it landed, with a note saying a
currency text role was a later decision. `OPEN_QUESTIONS.md` question 22 is why: the design pairs that
colour with `data-mono` in 65 places, and moving every price in the app into the mono face is a
composition judgement per surface rather than a metric one.

Decision 23 takes it for the till and for nothing else. `AppTextRoles.money` exists so a widget does
not hold a hex and so the next phase reads a name rather than copies a value — and the role's own doc
comment says outright that its existing is not permission to sweep it through the back office. The
grand total is the one figure that keeps the interface face: ST-035 sets it in `data-mono`, ST-036 in
`headline-lg-mobile`, so the two designs disagree about the face and agree about the colour. The half
they agree on moved.

### Three deviations, all deliberate, all recorded

The tile states `-3 in stock` where both designs write `Out of stock`: Firestore Rules permit signed
stock deliberately, the cached count really can be negative, and `0 in stock` says what the phrase says
while `-3 in stock` says something it cannot.

The price and the cached figure take two lines where ST-035 puts them on one. That row works at its
ten-pixel stock label; §2.1 makes `caption` at twelve the floor for anything a person is expected to
read, and the first attempt drew `KES 145.…` at 1024. An ellipsised price on a till is the one thing
this screen may not do.

The cart pane's three regions are divided by hairlines rather than by ST-035's surface step, and the
step is added back for the wide layout only, as an explicit argument. The same pane renders inside
`AppSheet`, whose ground is §2.1's `overlay` — a step *above* `raised` — so a `raised` header inside
one would draw recessed and invert the depth §2.1 is built on.

### One thing that had been wrong since before this run

The product tiles never filled their grid cells. `PressSurface.fillWidth` and `fillHeight` offer the
whole cell but pass *loose* constraints on, so a `MainAxisSize.min` column shrink-wrapped its own text
and sat centred in the middle of the box — four cards of four different widths with ragged gutters
between the rows — and the `Spacer` in the old tile was inert for exactly the same reason, because a
flex child of a `min` column has no space to take. Both bodies are `max` and `stretch` now.

### What moved, measured rather than estimated

**2,315 tests pass, from 2,314.** One test was added: the money role's value and its contrast on all
four grounds, which is §9 and therefore pass/fail rather than optional. Three copy assertions changed
and none of them is behaviour — the tile's price left the stock sentence and the compact bar's total
left the word, both because money takes a role of its own now and one `Text` cannot carry two roles.

**No behaviour test moved.** `test/checkout/` is 10,981 lines and every line passes unchanged, which is
the signal the handover asked for: a composition change that broke one of those would have meant a
state transition changed, and hard rule 1 is absolute.

The harness writes **413 images, from 405**: eight new, **seventeen moved, none removed** — and every
one of the seventeen is a `14`, `15` or `15b` till capture. Nothing outside the sale path moved, which
is the measurement that says the change is contained. Both figures are before-and-after `sha256sum`
over `screenshots/`, because that directory is gitignored and `git status` reports nothing whatever it
holds.

**What this proves is the raster.** No screen overflows or truncates at any of the five width regions,
which a widget test does detect and which cost four iterations on two tile heights and three layout
throws to reach. It does not prove the app runs. It cannot show motion: nothing here touched the save
or tender timing, so the sale path's rule — the sale is written first and the animation plays over
committed state — is where it was, which is *unchanged* rather than *verified*. Confirming that takes a
device with the performance overlay on.

**Nothing in Phase 03 is pixel-approved.** ST-035 is a reviewed candidate that no person has compared
to this implementation; ST-036 is `NORMALIZED / RENDER REVIEW`, corrected and never visually
confirmed; the browse render is recovered rather than approved.

## The catalog stops telling a cashier a product cannot be sold — 2026-08-22

Stitch Phase 04, catalog and stock: four commits, `f8a4095` to `1efe758`, on `stitch-wave-0-tokens`.
Three of the brief's four slices are done, the fourth is recorded as a derivation, and one route
inside it is deliberately not started. Nothing pushed, no PR, client-only — `git diff` over
`functions/`, `firestore.rules`, `rules-tests/`, `pubspec.yaml` and the lockfile prints nothing, so
those three suites were skipped rather than assumed.

**The slice that changed no Dart found the phase's only real defect.** That is the whole shape of this
session and it was the handover's own prediction: photograph what exists before changing it, because
it is the cheapest way to find out how much is already right.

### What the pictures were missing, and what they showed once taken

Thirteen catalog and stock routes rendered at 1440 and 411 and nowhere else. `RecordList.formFor` has
**three** forms — stacked cards below 768, two-column cards to 1023, a table at 1024 — so the middle
one, which is exactly what ST-039's section 8 draws an 834px specimen of, appeared in no picture of
any real route. The component's own matrix covered it; its use on a page of six columns and two
actions did not. And every management capture ran under `seedSession()`, which is owner, so the
role branch this phase is *about* had never been rendered at all.

`responsiveViewports` on the thirteen, plus three role captures that did not exist:
`17b-read-only-catalog-cashier`, `18d-manage-catalog-manager` and `19b-correct-a-product-manager`.
**71 new images, none of the existing 413 moved**, which is the measurement that says a no-Dart slice
only added coverage.

No route overflows or truncates at 834 or 1024 — the finding slice 1 was told to look for, and it is
a negative one. What the new pictures do show is worth more:

- The manager's correction form already states its own narrowing, in a notice
  (`catalog-management-edit-money-hidden`) that is very nearly ST-039's own sentence: *"Only an owner
  or administrator may change what this product is priced at or what it costs, so neither is offered
  here."* It had never been rasterised. Neither had the list's *"Only an owner or administrator may
  retire a product."*
- The cashier's catalog withholds all three stock routes and every row action **from the same build
  that offers them to an owner**. The screen decides, which is what makes the capture evidence rather
  than a build that withheld them.
- `23-stock-movements` contains both examples the live handoff asks ST-039 to show — the `+24` manual
  adjustment with reason `Morning delivery received` and the `-2` sale with source `co-1` — side by
  side in one picture. That was the one genuinely open fixture question in the handover and it is
  closed.

### The defect: a red badge that said the sale was blocked

`tenantProductStanding` gave every product at or below zero an `AppStatus.problem` badge reading
**`Out of stock`**, on both catalog surfaces, with nothing on either page to qualify it. `Milk 500ml`
at `-3` and `Water 1L` at `0` both wore it.

That phrase asserts a state this app does not have. Firestore Rules permit signed stock deliberately,
`OPEN_QUESTIONS.md`'s Phase 04 item 4 resolves stock as *"may be negative, and never blocks a sale"*,
and `audits/phase-04.md` records the same fact. Phase 03 had already refused these exact two words one
file over — `checkout_cart_panel.dart:1670` reasons that *"`0 in stock` says what `Out of stock` says;
`-3 in stock` says something it cannot"* — so the app was saying two different things about one
product fact on two screens, and Phase 04's second acceptance criterion is precisely that stock
display must not imply sales are blocked.

The catalog is where it mattered most, for two reasons the till does not have: it lists **every**
product, so the badge is the page's only summary of a zero figure; and it is the one catalog surface a
**cashier** sees, read-only, where a red badge is exactly what would stop somebody selling.

The badge label is the quantity now — `-3 in stock`, `0 in stock` — and each catalog surface states
ST-039's own sentence once under its product heading, from one constant. The app already ended two
other sentences with that clause (`checkout_cart_panel.dart:1282`,
`stock_adjustment_panel.dart:528`), so this is the established fact reaching the two screens that were
missing it rather than a third copy. `problem` is kept: §2.1 names *"out of stock"* among its
meanings, ST-039 draws this same row in error colour, and a figure at or below zero is genuinely worth
a correction. The colour was never the defect — the claim was. The reasoning, what it does not settle,
and why the sentence is a page line rather than a per-row warning are `OPEN_QUESTIONS.md`
**decision 24**.

**Two copy assertions moved and neither is behaviour. A third broke on layout**: the new caption line
pushed `View stock` to y=640 on an 800x600 test surface, and `tester.tap` *warns* rather than fails
when it misses, so what actually failed was the assertion after it. It scrolls first now, the way its
own sibling in the same file already did. 49 images moved, 0 new, 0 removed, and **all 49 are screens
17 to 19** — the bulk and stock routes did not move, which is what says the change is contained.

### The token debt, counted and cleared

`lib/inventory/` held **97 literal spacings** in widgets against two in `lib/ui/`. All 97 are gone,
and 94 of them are the same value the token names and moved no pixel — which is the point: a phase
that restyles a surface and leaves ninety-seven literals in it has not done the phase.

Three did move, and they are why it was worth looking. `catalog_management_panel.dart` separated its
four section headings at **two** different values, one at 24 and three at 28, and 28 is not on
`AppSpacing.all` at all — a list documented as *every* permitted value. The three take `s24`, which is
the value already doing that job in the same file and in `reconciliation_status_panel.dart` one
directory over. **40 of the 484 images moved and all 40 are the six management-catalog screens**, the
one file those gaps were in; nothing else in the app moved a pixel, which is the measurement that says
the other 94 repoints were value for value.

Two feed panels had expression-bodied builds with no `tokens` in scope and now read it as every other
panel does. One `const Padding` became a `Padding` around a `const Text`, because a token is not a
compile-time constant.

### Slice 3: keep all four, and the one measurement that mattered

The brief's third slice is the raw Material left on these screens — a `SegmentedButton` for Add stock
/ Remove stock, the category strip's `Chip`s, two `Checkbox`es, and the bulk report's `Card`.
**The finding is that none of them should change.** Every one is themed and reads the token layer:
`lib/theme.dart` has a `chipTheme`, a `checkboxTheme` and a `cardTheme`, and its `chipTheme` note
names the catalog's raw category list as the very site it was written for. `SegmentedButton` is
reached three ways, at `theme.dart:257` and `:322`. §5.2 specifies neither a segmented control nor a
checkbox, so building one is a component with a full state matrix — which is what Phase 03 declined
for the tender chooser.

What did need checking was §9, and **the guess was wrong**. The direction control looked like a 48dp
defect: Material draws a segmented button at 40 by default and `lib/theme.dart` has no
`segmentedButtonTheme` at all, so nothing in the token layer was holding it up. It draws at **48.0**.
The measurement is kept as an assertion in `test/theme_test.dart`, because
`test/ui/tokens_test.dart` asserts §9's floor only for the three button themes that have a
`minimumSize` to read and is silent on every widget family that does not — so nothing would notice a
later `segmentedButtonTheme` arriving under the floor.

### The four ST-039 defects, and the app was already right about all four

Checked against the code at `7d54e28` rather than taken from the handover's table, which is what its
own §8 trap asks for. Three separate routes rather than one collapsed table; `Before and after` from
one named constant with two call sites; a `provenance:` line carrying actor and recorded time on both
record builders; and no placeholder at all on the reason field. **Four for four**, the same shape
Phases 02 and 03 each found twice — the app is right where the design is wrong — and no code was
written for any of them.

### Slice 4, and the route that was not started

ST-040 is **9,218 bytes and one section of nine**, and `EXPORT_MAP.md` uses that byte count as a
freshness fingerprint, so the truncation is the artifact rather than a failed download. There is no
Stitch connector in this session and mutation needs human authorisation, so the missing eight sections
cannot be generated. Phase 04's mobile records are therefore `RecordList`'s own responsive contract,
**recorded as a derivation** in `OPEN_QUESTIONS.md` decision 25 — the derivation being ST-039's
section 8 rendered through the contract that specimen is a picture of, now photographed at all four
widths rather than asserted.

**Screens 20, 20b and 20c were not migrated and are the phase's unfinished route.** Their rows are
`CheckboxListTile`s whose subtitle is a bullet-separated sentence — `Household ▪ 5901234123457 ▪
145.00 ▪ costs 112.00`, the pre-migration shape §5.2 replaces with key-value attributes — and the
report rows below them are raw `Card`s. The note already at `bulk_catalog_panel.dart` reaches the same
conclusion this session did: migrating screen 20 to `RecordList` is the work step 6 did for twelve
screens, and it is larger than a Phase 04 slice. Cut deliberately rather than half-done.

### Two figures in the handover that were wrong, and one deviation of this session's own

- `PHASE_04_HANDOVER.md` says `lib/checkout/` holds seven literal spacings and *"all seven of those
  are in `checkout_configuration_panel.dart`"*. The count is right and the attribution is not: **six**
  are there and the seventh is `checkout_evidence.dart:311`, which is Phase 02's checkout-evidence
  surface rather than screen 16's. It is a real hard-rule-2 site with no phase currently claiming it.
- The same document, and `PHASE_03_HANDOVER.md` before it, says to update *"the Current state table in
  `prompt.md`"*. **`prompt.md` has no Current state table** — it is the instruction prompt, its own
  first line points at `PLAN.md`, and its last content change was an unrelated commit. `PLAN.md` is
  the state file and its Flutter baseline was two chunks stale, reading 2314 when Phase 03 had left it
  at 2315. Corrected there instead.
- **This session's own deviation**: `dart format` on the two test files the badge change touched
  reflowed about 200 lines that have nothing to do with it, and the handover's instruction is to
  commit that reflow alone first. `06472ad` carries both. The split was attempted and the `git reset`
  it needed was declined, so it stands — read that commit's two test files knowing most of their diff
  is reflow.

### Testing, and what it proves

**2,316 tests pass, from 2,315.** One test added and it is the §9 case, which is pass/fail rather
than optional. **No behaviour test moved**: `test/inventory/` is 9,345 lines and all 272 of its tests
pass unchanged, and the three assertions that did change are two copy strings and one `tap` that now
scrolls first. The harness writes **484 images across 158 screens, from 413 across 155** — 71 new, 89
moved across the two Dart commits, 0 removed, every moved image a screen between 17 and 19. Both
figures are before-and-after `sha256sum` over `screenshots/`, because that directory is gitignored and
`git status` reports nothing whatever it holds.

**What this proves is the raster.** It does not prove the app runs. It cannot show motion, and nothing
here touched any, so the sale path's rule is where Phase 03 left it — *unchanged* rather than
*verified*. The catalog's new caption line and the relabelled badge have never been read on a physical
screen; the raster is right at all four widths, and a device is what would show whether the sentence
reads as standing context or as noise.

**Nothing in Phase 04 is pixel-approved.** ST-039 is `NORMALIZED / RENDER REVIEW` *and* the export is
its pre-correction render, so no part of this implementation has been compared against an approved
artifact by a person. ST-040 does not meaningfully exist. Decision 24's badge wording is this run's
and not the design's: ST-039 puts `Below zero. A sale is never blocked by a stock count.` inline under
a product name, and this is the quantity in a badge plus the sentence once per page. The clause is the
design's; the arrangement is not.

## The pill comes back, and the last literal spacing goes — 2026-08-23

Thirteen commits, `fd247c4` to `d0f54fa`, on `stitch-wave-0-tokens`. Three strands: Phase 07's
evidence and token slices, three product-owner shape directions applied across the whole app, and the
end of hard rule 2's spacing debt. Nothing pushed, no PR, client-only.

### Phase 07: the forms nobody had photographed, and what that hid

`tenant_staff_directory.dart` offers six actions and exactly one of them had a capture. The whole
staff family had three images, against a brief asking for pending, active, disabled, expired/invalid,
busy, validation and failure states — and ST-055's fourth section draws a consequence dialog for
every one of the five with none. The behaviour was never the thin part: eleven test files, 5,501
lines, 122 tests, all passing. What was missing was the raster.

The first attempt at those captures failed at 411 and 834, and the reason is worth keeping. §4.3 folds
a row's actions into an overflow menu below 1024, and `RecordActionSet.inlineCountFor` draws **no**
action inline on stacked cards once a record carries more than three. A pending membership has four —
correct, resend, cancel, replace — so all four are behind the menu on a phone and the fourth is behind
it on a tablet. `13b` never had to deal with that because an accepted membership carries two, which is
precisely why photographing one action was not photographing the route.

**What the pictures then showed was a copy defect that had been in every `13b` image ever taken.** The
row action says `Correct`; the form it opened said `Edit`. §8 rule 4 is the rule it breaks in as many
words — *"The verb persists. The button says Correct, the dialog says Correct"* — and it was the only
one of the five forms that broke it. The other four already carry the verb of the action that opened
them, and ST-055 writes the heading `Correct Staff: {name}`, so the design and the rule agreed and the
app disagreed with both. Nobody had noticed because there was nothing beside it to compare against.
That is twice in two phases that adding coverage rather than reading code surfaced the defect.

Phase 07's own composition slice is **not started**. The new captures show the app already matches
ST-055 closely — every form names its person and consequence, the manager's reading carries no write
affordance at any width, the tablet transformation holds — and two divergences are recorded as
divergences rather than defects: the app draws a four-tile stat strip ST-055 has none of, and splits
its combined `STATUS + MEMBERSHIP` column into a badge and an attribute.

One finding is left open on purpose. On stacked cards a record with more than three actions draws no
label at all, just an unlabelled vertical-dots control — and `_staffActions`' own comment says these
were once "a 40dp `IconButton` with the member's name in a tooltip and no visible label" which §5.2's
`ActionSet` fixed. At the compact band it is still an icon-only control. The fix is in `RecordList`,
which every record surface reads, so it is a Wave 3 item and not a Phase 07 slice.

### A day boundary that cost a bisect

`seedBusinessDate` and `seedTimestamp` read the wall clock, deliberately and for a documented reason:
the daily summary and reconciliation compute the same string from `DateTime.now()` and read by exact
path, so a hardcoded fixture date renders them permanently empty. What nobody had written down is the
consequence for the way every phase here proves a change is contained. "N images moved" is that
evidence, and it holds only inside one UTC day.

This session crossed midnight between a baseline hash and a re-measure. A nine-file spacing repoint
appeared to move 36 reporting, shift, returns and receipt images — none of which it had touched —
and against a same-day baseline it moved **zero**. The note at the fixture now says what the tell is
(the moved set is all date-bearing screens and contains nothing you edited) and what to do
(re-baseline, do not hunt your own diff). Fixing it properly needs one injectable clock shared by the
fixtures and the surfaces under test, which is a behaviour change.

### Three shapes the product owner chose

Recorded as `OPEN_QUESTIONS.md` decision 26, and recorded as **overrides** rather than readings of the
design, because two of them reverse a decision that argued from evidence. Profound Verdant's own CSS
gives `.btn-primary` and its inputs `borderRadius.xl`, its status chips carry a bare `rounded` in 78
of the 82 places one appears, and its rendered screens are square-cornered throughout. That is what
moved buttons, chips and wells off the pill on 2026-08-22. A shape is the owner's to choose; what the
record owes a later reader is the evidence it overrides, so nobody re-derives the old answer and files
a regression.

**The pill is back** on `AppButton`, `FilterChipBar`'s chip, the `AppTextField` well, the three
Material button themes, `chipTheme` and the theme's `InputDecoration` border — and deliberately not on
cards, rows, dialogs, sheets, banners, stat tiles, the snack bar or `StatusBadge`. A badge is read
rather than pressed and was never a pill, and Flutter clamps a radius to half the shorter side, so 999
on a wide card draws a lozenge. The token values themselves did not move: `sm` is still 2, `md` 8,
`lg` 12, `pill` 999, and what changed is only which component reads which role. **417 of 536 images
moved**, which is the right blast radius. For the input well it is the third move of one value — v0.4
made it a pill at the owner's request, 2026-08-22 took it back, this restores it.

**Multi-filter surfaces are dropdowns now.** Sales totals is the one the direction is about and the
only surface in the app with three filters open at once; as chip strips their height grew with the
business, one chip per colleague and one per category, so twelve staff and nine categories pushed the
figures the page exists for off the bottom of a phone. The three figures now sit on the first screen.
A single filter stays a chip strip, which is the other half of the same rule — one strip shows its
options without a tap. `AppSelectItem` gained a `key` so that moving a filter between the two did not
silently drop every option-level contract the surface had; all nine keys are unchanged.

Two test mechanics there were worth getting right rather than working around. Choosing an option taps
the option's `Text`, not its `DropdownMenuItem`: a closed `DropdownButton` keeps an offstage copy of
the *selected* item, so `.last` on the key sometimes picked the button's copy over the menu's — and
tapping an offstage widget warns instead of failing, which left four tests asserting against a filter
nobody had changed. `hitTestable()` does not help; the menu item is not its own hit target. And label
assertions now read `AppSelect.items` rather than the rendering, the reverse of what that file used to
do and for the same underlying reason: the chip was private so only its `Text` was visible, and the
dropdown's rendering is what has become conditional.

**One cost of that is stated rather than left to be found:** a dropdown's options are not in a
screenshot. A closed dropdown builds only the selected option, so hard rule 5's coverage is weaker
here than for the chip strip it replaced, where every option was always rendered.

**The password field shows eight asterisks.** It carried no placeholder from step 9 until now, on
reasoning that was right about the string it deleted — `Enter Password` restates the label — and wrong
to conclude the field could therefore carry nothing. Asterisks are the permitted kind: they are what
the box looks like once somebody types in it. `AppTextField` gained `obscuringCharacter`, defaulting to
an asterisk for every obscured field, because a placeholder showing asterisks over a field that types
bullets is a box that appears to change character set the moment it is touched.

### The end of the spacing debt

228 literal spacings have now been removed across three phases: 97 in `lib/inventory/`, 39 across the
staff surfaces, and the last **92** across 41 files — the platform-admin family, the sales, returns,
shift and audit histories, the routing shell, and eight `lib/ui/` components. There are none left
outside the token layer.

Three of them were decisions rather than mechanics. `SizedBox(height: 10)` takes `s8`, which groups
the error with the field it belongs to. `cardTheme`'s `vertical: 6` margin takes `s4` — equidistant
from 4 and 8, and 4 wins because the margin applies on both sides so it is the gap *between* two cards
that doubles. And `EdgeInsets.fromLTRB(20, 20, 20, 0)`'s zero stays a literal zero, because an inset
of nothing is not a spacing and `AppSpacing` rightly has no token for it.

Three non-moves matter as much. `lib/ui/tokens.dart` keeps its own literals, because `AppDensity`'s
two `rowPadding` values are the token layer stating its own numbers and a layer that read itself from
somewhere else would have nowhere to bottom out. `lib/theme.dart` reads a new `_spacing` off the
registered palette rather than a `tokens` that has no meaning at top level, which is the same shape as
the `_palette`, `_action` and `_surface` aliases beside it. And comment lines are untouched
throughout: several files document a spacing that used to be there, and rewriting the prose would be a
lie about history.

`test/dev/token_spacing_test.dart` holds it, and was verified by breaking it — a planted
`SizedBox(height: 12)` is reported with its file and line, and the failure message carries the scale,
the rule for an off-scale value, and the two mechanical traps this work paid for: an expression-bodied
`build` has no `tokens` in scope, and `const` around a token does not compile. The pattern is
deliberately narrow, matching the two constructors that carry essentially all of this app's spacing;
one that also flagged `Size(48, 48)` and every `elevation: 0` would be a scan people silence rather
than obey.

### What this does not finish

**Phases 09, 06, 05 and 08 have had no composition pass, Phase 10 has not been run, and Phases 01 and
02 still need the visual pass their structural check at `06a24f9` left them.** Phase 07's slice 3 is
not started either. The token layer, the harness's width coverage and the three owner shapes now reach
all of those surfaces, so none of that work will need redoing — but none of it is done, and the reskin
is not finished. 2,318 tests pass and the harness writes 536 images across 163 screens; what that
proves is the raster, and no part of this implementation has been compared to a design by a person.
